This includes clearly readable:

• Product name
• Brand name
• Nutritional values
• Product specifications
• Flavor
• Weight
• Product features
• Printed claims

ONLY use information that is clearly supported by the uploaded image or explicitly provided by the user.

Do NOT invent:

• nutritional facts
• ingredients
• calories
• protein percentages
• health claims
• medical claims
• prices
• discounts
• certifications
• awards
• statistics
• testimonials
• product specifications
• performance claims

Do not create marketing claims that are not supported by the packaging.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
8. FACTUAL ACCURACY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

This is CRITICAL.

Every factual product statement in the advertisement must be traceable to either:

1. The uploaded product packaging
   OR
2. Information explicitly provided by the user.

Never fill missing information with assumptions.

Never use generic supplement statistics.

Never invent benefits simply because the product belongs to a particular category.

For example:

Do NOT automatically claim:

"Builds muscle"
"Burns fat"
"Boosts testosterone"
"Improves recovery"
"Clinically proven"
"100% pure"
"Zero sugar"
"High absorption"

unless the claim is explicitly visible on the packaging or explicitly provided by the user.

Accuracy is more important than adding more text.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
9. LANGUAGE HANDLING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Detect the primary language of the product packaging and user-provided information.

Preserve the original product name and brand exactly when appropriate.

If the advertisement requires supporting text, use the language appropriate to the provided product information.

Do NOT translate the product brand or product name unless explicitly requested.

If the packaging contains Arabic information, preserve Arabic wording accurately.

If the packaging contains English information, preserve English wording accurately.

Do NOT introduce unnecessary bilingual text.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
10. CORE GLASSMORPHISM DIRECTION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a sophisticated PREMIUM GLASSMORPHISM visual system.

The glass must feel:

• translucent
• physically believable
• soft
• elegant
• dimensional
• refined
• lightweight
• futuristic

Use glass as a structural visual language rather than a decorative effect.

The design should feel like a premium next-generation fitness technology or luxury sports-nutrition campaign.

Use layered transparent surfaces to create depth.

Use subtle:

• frosted glass
• translucent panels
• soft blur
• background diffusion
• edge highlights
• subtle refraction
• light transmission
• controlled transparency
• layered depth
• soft reflections

Every glass element must have a purpose.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
11. PRODUCT PRIORITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The product MUST remain more visually important than every glass element.

Glass is the supporting visual system.

The product must NOT become visually obscured by excessive transparency, blur, reflections, or overlays.

The product must remain:

• sharp
• recognizable
• readable
• visually dominant
• physically grounded

Do not place strong glass effects directly over important product details.

Do not blur the product.

Do not reduce product clarity.

The glass environment should frame the product rather than hide it.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
12. VISUAL HIERARCHY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Establish a strict visual hierarchy:

1. PRODUCT
2. PRODUCT TITLE / PRIMARY MESSAGE
3. KEY PRODUCT INFORMATION
4. BRAND
5. SUPPORTING INFORMATION
6. CTA, if provided

The product must immediately attract attention.

Typography must remain secondary.

Glass surfaces must remain tertiary.

Decorative elements must remain almost invisible.

The viewer should understand the advertisement within approximately one second.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
13. GLASS MATERIAL
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create physically believable glass surfaces.

Glass panels should have:

• subtle transparency
• soft frosted blur
• realistic edge definition
• gentle internal light diffusion
• subtle highlights
• controlled reflections
• realistic depth
• delicate borders

Avoid making the glass look like plastic.

Avoid making the glass look like acrylic blocks.

Avoid excessive transparency.

Avoid excessive opacity.

Use a sophisticated balance between visibility and translucency.

Glass should reveal the background behind it while softly diffusing it.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
14. FROSTED GLASS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use premium frosted-glass behavior.

Glass surfaces should subtly blur and diffuse whatever appears behind them.

The blur should be:

• soft
• controlled
• realistic
• localized

Do NOT apply the same blur strength everywhere.

Vary the blur subtly according to depth.

The glass must still feel transparent.

Do not turn the background into an unreadable blur.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
15. GLASS EDGES
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use extremely subtle glass edges.

Possible characteristics:

• thin luminous edge
• soft white highlight
• subtle specular line
• faint translucent border

Edges should be visible only when light interacts with them.

Do NOT use thick borders.

Do NOT use neon outlines.

Do NOT create glowing UI panels.

The edge treatment must feel physical and elegant.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
16. GLASS REFRACTION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Introduce subtle realistic optical distortion where appropriate.

Glass may slightly distort background elements.

Use:

• subtle refraction
• slight displacement
• gentle light bending
• controlled transparency variation

The distortion must remain extremely subtle.

Never distort:

• product packaging
• logos
• important typography
• faces
• important objects

The purpose is to create physical realism, not visual chaos.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
17. BACKGROUND
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a sophisticated atmospheric background designed specifically to support Glassmorphism.

Prefer:

• dark charcoal
• deep black
• soft gray
• cool neutral tones
• subtle brand colors
• muted gradients
• atmospheric lighting
• soft luminous zones

Extract the dominant visual colors from the actual product packaging and use them as subtle environmental accents.

The background should contain enough tonal variation for the glass surfaces to be visible.

However, it must remain visually quiet.

Avoid complicated scenery.

Avoid realistic gyms unless explicitly requested.

Avoid excessive objects.

Avoid dramatic environments.

The background exists primarily to create depth behind the glass.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
18. LIGHTING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use sophisticated cinematic studio lighting combined with premium digital lighting.

Lighting should interact naturally with:

• product
• glass
• background
• translucent surfaces

Create:

• soft highlights
• subtle reflections
• gentle rim lighting
• realistic contact shadows
• controlled light falloff
• soft atmospheric illumination

Light should reveal the glass.

Do NOT create excessive glow.

Do NOT use aggressive neon lighting.

Do NOT make everything luminous.

The lighting must remain elegant and controlled.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
19. PRODUCT LIGHTING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Treat the product as a premium commercial photography subject.

Use professional product lighting.

The product must have:

• realistic highlights
• realistic shadows
• accurate material response
• dimensional form
• sharp edges
• realistic contact with the environment

Create subtle separation between product and background.

The product should appear physically present inside the Glassmorphism environment.

It should NOT look like a flat image pasted onto the design.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
20. GLASS LAYERING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a carefully controlled depth hierarchy.

Possible layers:

BACKGROUND
↓
ATMOSPHERIC LIGHT
↓
DISTANT GLASS
↓
MIDGROUND GLASS
↓
PRODUCT
↓
FOREGROUND GLASS ACCENTS
↓
TYPOGRAPHY

Do NOT use all layers heavily.

Some layers may be extremely subtle.

Use depth to create a sophisticated three-dimensional environment.

The product should remain the strongest focal point.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
21. GLASS PANELS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use a LIMITED number of glass panels.

Each panel should have a purpose.

Possible uses:

• framing the product
• containing key nutritional information
• containing a headline
• containing a CTA
• creating depth
• separating information
• adding subtle visual structure

Do NOT cover the entire canvas with glass cards.

Do NOT create a dashboard.

Do NOT make the design look like a website UI.

This is a COMMERCIAL ADVERTISEMENT, not an application interface.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
22. INFORMATION CALLOUTS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

When reliable nutritional or product information has been extracted from the packaging, present the most important values as elegant visual callouts.

Examples:

27g PROTEIN
109 KCAL
86% PROTEIN
1 KG

These are ONLY examples of formatting.

Do not automatically use these numbers unless they are actually visible on the uploaded product packaging.

Use clean, minimal typography.

Use small glass surfaces or subtle floating information elements where appropriate.

Do not turn the advertisement into an infographic.

Do not display too many numbers.

Maximum visual information should remain concise and premium.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
23. DISTRACTION CONTROL
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

THIS IS CRITICAL.

The advertisement must remain extremely easy on the eyes.

Glassmorphism can quickly become visually noisy.

Avoid that.

DO NOT add:

• excessive glass cards
• dozens of translucent shapes
• random floating circles
• excessive bubbles
• random 3D objects
• excessive reflections
• excessive blur
• excessive glow
• neon grids
• random particles
• lightning
• smoke
• fire
• explosions
• unnecessary gym equipment
• random dumbbells
• random weights
• bodybuilding silhouettes
• unrelated athletes
• excessive decorative elements
• fake statistics
• fake product claims
• fake certifications
• unnecessary icons

If an element does not improve the product presentation, REMOVE IT.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
24. COLOR SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Build the color system around the actual product packaging.

Extract the dominant colors from the product.

Use those colors as subtle environmental accents.

Maintain a restrained palette.

Prefer:

• one dominant background tone
• product colors
• translucent white or neutral glass
• one subtle accent color

Do not introduce unrelated colors.

The glass should generally remain:

• clear
• frosted
• translucent
• neutral

unless a very subtle brand tint improves the composition.

Avoid rainbow glass.

Avoid excessive multicolor effects.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
25. TYPOGRAPHY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use premium modern typography.

Typography should be:

• clean
• minimal
• sophisticated
• highly readable
• balanced
• contemporary

Use no more than TWO typefaces.

Prefer:

• modern sans-serif
• geometric sans-serif
• neo-grotesk
• clean editorial typography

Typography should have strong contrast against glass.

Never allow text to disappear into transparency.

Use subtle shadows or contrast only when necessary for readability.

Do NOT use:

• decorative fonts
• excessive outlines
• glowing text
• metallic text
• extreme gradients
• excessive text effects

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
26. TEXT DENSITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Keep the amount of text LOW.

This is a premium commercial advertisement, NOT a product catalog, nutrition label, or flyer.

Do not copy the entire back label into the design.

Do not display every ingredient or nutritional value.

Select only the strongest, most useful information.

Prioritize visual impact and immediate comprehension.

Use short labels and concise information.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
27. FITNESS / NUTRITION VISUAL LANGUAGE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Communicate fitness through modern sophistication.

Possible concepts:

• performance
• athletic precision
• clean energy
• strength
• discipline
• wellness
• recovery
• technology
• innovation
• premium sports culture

Glassmorphism should reinforce a sense of:

NEXT-GENERATION PERFORMANCE.

Do not automatically add gym equipment.

Do not automatically add athletes.

Do not use bodybuilding clichés unless explicitly requested.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
28. NEGATIVE SPACE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Maintain generous breathing room.

Glassmorphism requires controlled negative space.

Do not fill empty areas with random glass elements.

Empty space should create:

• elegance
• focus
• clarity
• visual breathing room
• premium perception

The design should feel spacious rather than crowded.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
29. COMPOSITION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use professional commercial composition.

Possible approaches:

• central hero
• asymmetric editorial composition
• rule-of-thirds
• vertical product emphasis
• layered depth composition
• controlled diagonal flow

Choose the strongest composition automatically based on the product image and extracted information.

Do not mechanically follow a template.

The composition must feel custom-designed for the specific product.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
30. BRANDING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

If a brand name or logo is clearly visible on the product:

Integrate it subtly.

Do not overpower the product.

Do not redesign the logo.

Do not invent brand elements.

Maintain visual consistency with the product packaging.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
31. PREMIUM COMMERCIAL QUALITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The final advertisement should feel suitable for:

• premium sports nutrition brands
• luxury fitness brands
• modern wellness companies
• athletic technology brands
• high-end supplement companies
• professional social-media campaigns

Think:

LUXURY FITNESS TECHNOLOGY
+
PREMIUM SPORTS NUTRITION
+
HIGH-END GLASSMORPHISM
+
COMMERCIAL PRODUCT PHOTOGRAPHY

Do NOT make it look like:

• a generic AI poster
• a cheap supplement ad
• a gaming poster
• a UI mockup
• a mobile app screen
• a cryptocurrency advertisement
• a futuristic sci-fi poster
• a crowded Instagram template

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
32. IMAGE QUALITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Prioritize extremely high visual quality.

The final artwork must have:

• photorealistic product presentation
• accurate packaging
• realistic glass
• realistic transparency
• realistic refraction
• realistic reflections
• realistic shadows
• physically believable lighting
• clean edges
• sharp product details
• sophisticated depth
• professional color grading
• premium art direction
• polished typography
• commercial-quality finish

Avoid:

• warped packaging
• distorted logos
• duplicated products
• malformed objects
• unreadable text
• excessive blur
• fake glass
• plastic-looking glass
• unrealistic reflections
• excessive bloom
• inconsistent perspective
• AI artifacts
• invented product information

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
33. FINAL ART-DIRECTION CHECK
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Before finalizing the artwork, evaluate it as a professional commercial art director.

Ask:

Is the product immediately recognizable?

Is the product the strongest visual element?

Did the product analysis use only information actually visible in the uploaded image?

Are all nutritional values and specifications accurate?

Did the design avoid invented claims?

Does the Glassmorphism feel premium and physically believable?

Does the glass support the product rather than compete with it?

Is the background visually quiet?

Is there enough negative space?

Is the typography readable?

Are the extracted product details easy to understand?

Is there too much information?

Does the design feel futuristic without becoming cliché?

Are there too many glass elements?

Can anything be removed to make the design cleaner?

Does the composition feel expensive?

Would a real premium fitness or nutrition brand publish this?

If removing an element makes the composition stronger, REMOVE IT.

The final design must feel:

GLASSY.
TRANSLUCENT.
PREMIUM.
FUTURISTIC.
CLEAN.
ELEGANT.
MINIMAL.
DIMENSIONAL.
SOPHISTICATED.
COMMERCIAL.
EASY ON THE EYES.

The goal is NOT to demonstrate how many Glassmorphism effects can be added.

The goal is to use Glassmorphism with enough restraint that the product feels elevated by the environment.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
34. FINAL OUTPUT
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Generate ONE finished advertisement.

Do not generate multiple variations.

Do not show sketches.

Do not show wireframes.

Do not provide explanations.

Analyze the uploaded product image first, extract the reliable product information, select the most valuable information, and then generate the final polished commercial artwork directly.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
35. ASPECT RATIO — CHANGE ONLY THIS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

FINAL ASPECT RATIO:

9:16 VERTICAL PORTRAIT

Design the entire composition specifically for this aspect ratio from the beginning.

Do NOT create another aspect ratio and crop it afterward.

Do NOT stretch, squeeze, or distort the composition.

All visual elements must be intentionally positioned for the specified vertical format.

Maintain safe margins around the product, typography, logo, nutritional callouts, and all important elements.

The final artwork must be a true 9:16 vertical composition optimized for Instagram Stories, Reels, and vertical social-media presentation.

prompts.title: Glassmorphisim Ar
prompts.promptText:
Create a premium commercial FITNESS / NUTRITION advertisement using a STRICT, SOPHISTICATED, HIGH-END GLASSMORPHISM DESIGN STYLE.

The final artwork must be designed specifically for an ARABIC-SPEAKING AUDIENCE.

Arabic must be the PRIMARY visual language of the final advertisement.

The final artwork must look like it was created by an elite commercial art director, premium fitness brand designer, professional product photographer, Arabic typography specialist, and high-end digital visual designer working together.

The result must feel:

FUTURISTIC.
PREMIUM.
CLEAN.
ELEGANT.
LIGHTWEIGHT.
TRANSLUCENT.
MODERN.
SOPHISTICATED.
COMMERCIAL.
ARABIC-FIRST.
EASY ON THE EYES.

This is NOT a generic "glass effect" poster.

Do NOT simply place transparent rectangles behind the product.

Create a genuine, professionally art-directed Glassmorphism composition with realistic translucent surfaces, controlled blur, subtle refraction, soft highlights, layered depth, carefully managed transparency, and premium Arabic visual communication.

The PRODUCT remains the HERO.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1. PRODUCT INPUT
   ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

PRODUCT IMAGE:

[INSERT PRODUCT IMAGE]

The uploaded product image is the PRIMARY SOURCE OF TRUTH.

The image must be analyzed before creating the advertisement.

Do NOT require the user to manually provide product information if it can be reliably extracted from the uploaded image.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
2. PRODUCT IMAGE ANALYSIS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Before designing the advertisement, carefully inspect the uploaded product image.

Identify and extract ONLY information that is clearly visible and reliably readable from the product packaging.

Analyze:

• Product name
• Product type
• Brand name
• Flavor
• Net weight
• Serving size
• Protein amount per serving
• Calories per serving
• Protein percentage
• Carbohydrates
• Fat
• Ingredients
• Key nutritional information
• Product features
• Product claims
• Certifications
• Any other clearly printed product information

The uploaded packaging is the authoritative source.

Do NOT invent, assume, estimate, infer, or fabricate product information.

If information is partially visible but cannot be read with confidence, DO NOT use it.

If information is completely absent from the image, DO NOT create it.

If nutritional information is visible, preserve the exact values and units shown on the packaging.

Do not convert, reinterpret, round, or modify numerical values unless explicitly requested.

For example:

If the package says "27g Protein", the advertisement may present the factual information in Arabic context as:

"27 غ بروتين"

but the numerical value itself must remain exactly 27g.

If it says "109 kcal", use:

"109 سعرة حرارية"

without changing the number.

If it says "1 KG", use the equivalent Arabic presentation such as:

"1 كغ"

only when appropriate for the Arabic advertisement, while preserving the factual value.

Do not change factual values.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
3. INFORMATION SELECTION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

After analyzing the product image, automatically determine which extracted information is most valuable for a premium commercial advertisement.

Prioritize:

1. Product name
2. Brand name
3. Most important nutritional value
4. Key product specification
5. Net weight
6. Flavor, if relevant
7. One or two important product features

Do NOT attempt to display every piece of information extracted from the packaging.

This is a PREMIUM ADVERTISEMENT, not a nutrition facts sheet.

Select only the information that improves the advertisement.

Use concise Arabic visual callouts instead of paragraphs.

For example, if clearly visible on the package, information such as:

27g Protein
109 kcal
86% Protein
1 KG

may be transformed into elegant Arabic visual callouts such as:

27 غ بروتين
109 سعرة حرارية
86% بروتين
1 كغ

Only use these values if they are actually visible and readable in the uploaded image.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
4. PRODUCT TITLE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Automatically determine the product title from the uploaded packaging.

Use the exact recognizable product name printed on the package whenever possible.

Do NOT invent a new product name.

Do NOT rewrite the brand or product name unnecessarily.

If the product title is clearly written in English or another language as part of the official product identity, preserve the official product name.

Do NOT translate a brand name or official product name merely for the sake of translation.

If the product title contains generic descriptive wording that is appropriate to translate for the Arabic advertisement, translate it naturally while preserving the original meaning.

If the product title is unclear, use only the clearly readable portion.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
5. BRAND IDENTIFICATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Automatically identify the brand from the packaging if clearly visible.

Preserve the original logo and brand identity.

Do NOT redesign the logo.

Do NOT recreate a fake logo.

Do NOT invent brand elements.

Do NOT translate the official brand name unless explicitly requested.

The brand should remain visually consistent with the original packaging.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
6. PRODUCT PRESERVATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use the provided product image as the PRIMARY VISUAL SOURCE.

The product is the central visual hero of the entire composition.

Do NOT unnecessarily redesign, deform, replace, recolor, or alter the product packaging.

Preserve:

• exact product shape
• packaging structure
• logo
• brand identity
• printed typography
• label details
• proportions
• colors
• recognizable characteristics
• material appearance

The product must remain immediately recognizable as the exact original product.

If the provided image contains multiple products, preserve the correct number of products.

Do not duplicate products unnecessarily.

Do not generate additional flavors, variants, containers, packages, or accessories unless they are visibly present in the uploaded image.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
7. TEXT GENERATION RULES
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The advertisement may use TWO primary sources of text:

SOURCE A — USER-PROVIDED TEXT

If the user explicitly provides promotional text, CTA, price, offer, slogan, or campaign message, it may be incorporated into the design.

If the user-provided promotional text is in English but the final advertisement is intended for an Arabic-speaking audience, translate it naturally into professional Arabic unless the user explicitly requests English.

SOURCE B — PRODUCT-PACKAGING INFORMATION

The AI may extract factual product information directly from the uploaded packaging.

This includes clearly readable:

• Product name
• Brand name
• Nutritional values
• Product specifications
• Flavor
• Weight
• Product features
• Printed claims

ONLY use information that is clearly supported by the uploaded image or explicitly provided by the user.

All newly generated marketing text must be written in NATURAL, PROFESSIONAL, CORRECT ARABIC.

Do NOT invent:

• nutritional facts
• ingredients
• calories
• protein percentages
• health claims
• medical claims
• prices
• discounts
• certifications
• awards
• statistics
• testimonials
• product specifications
• performance claims

Do not create marketing claims that are not supported by the packaging or user-provided information.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
8. FACTUAL ACCURACY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

This is CRITICAL.

Every factual product statement in the advertisement must be traceable to either:

1. The uploaded product packaging

OR

2. Information explicitly provided by the user.

Never fill missing information with assumptions.

Never use generic supplement statistics.

Never invent benefits simply because the product belongs to a particular category.

For example:

Do NOT automatically claim:

"يساعد على بناء العضلات"

"يحرق الدهون"

"يعزز هرمون التستوستيرون"

"يسرّع الاستشفاء"

"مثبت سريريًا"

"نقي 100%"

"خالي من السكر"

"امتصاص سريع"

unless the claim is explicitly visible on the packaging or explicitly provided by the user.

Accuracy is more important than adding more text.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
9. LANGUAGE HANDLING

All newly generated:

• subtitles
• promotional messages
• CTAs
• supporting text
• product information callouts

must be written in professional Arabic.

Use NATURAL MODERN ARABIC suitable for commercial fitness and nutrition advertising.

Use correct:

• Arabic spelling
• Arabic grammar
• punctuation
• RTL direction
• Arabic letter connections
• Arabic typography
• text hierarchy

Do NOT generate pseudo-Arabic text.

Do NOT generate meaningless Arabic-like characters.

Do NOT reverse Arabic letters.

Do NOT mirror Arabic words incorrectly.

Do NOT place Arabic text using incorrect left-to-right direction.

All Arabic text must be properly readable from RIGHT TO LEFT.

The visual composition must also respect RTL reading flow.

The viewer's eye should naturally move through the design in a way that feels appropriate for Arabic visual communication.

Do NOT introduce unnecessary bilingual text.

English should only remain when it is part of:

• the original product packaging
• the official brand identity
• the official product name
• a user-provided element that the user explicitly wants preserved

• physically believable
• soft
• elegant
• dimensional
• refined
• lightweight
• futuristic

Use glass as a structural visual language rather than a decorative effect.

Use subtle:

• frosted glass
• translucent panels
• soft blur
• background diffusion
• edge highlights
• subtle refraction
• light transmission
• controlled transparency
• layered depth
• soft reflections

Every glass element must have a purpose.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
12. PRODUCT PRIORITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The product must remain:

• recognizable
• readable
• visually dominant
• physically grounded

Do not blur the product.

Do not reduce product clarity.

The glass environment should frame the product rather than hide it.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
13. VISUAL HIERARCHY

2. ARABIC PRODUCT TITLE / PRIMARY MESSAGE

4. BRAND
5. SUPPORTING INFORMATION
6. CTA, if provided

Arabic typography must remain secondary to the product.

Glass surfaces must remain tertiary.

Decorative elements must remain almost invisible.

The viewer should understand the advertisement within approximately one second.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
14. GLASS MATERIAL
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create physically believable glass surfaces.

Glass panels should have:

• subtle transparency
• soft frosted blur
• realistic edge definition
• gentle internal light diffusion
• subtle highlights
• controlled reflections
• realistic depth
• delicate borders

Avoid making the glass look like plastic.

Avoid making the glass look like acrylic blocks.

Avoid excessive transparency.

Avoid excessive opacity.

Use a sophisticated balance between visibility and translucency.

Glass should reveal the background behind it while softly diffusing it.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
15. FROSTED GLASS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use premium frosted-glass behavior.

Glass surfaces should subtly blur and diffuse whatever appears behind them.

The blur should be:

• soft
• controlled
• realistic
• localized

Do NOT apply the same blur strength everywhere.

Vary the blur subtly according to depth.

The glass must still feel transparent.

Do not turn the background into an unreadable blur.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
16. GLASS EDGES
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Possible characteristics:

• thin luminous edge
• soft white highlight
• subtle specular line
• faint translucent border

Do NOT use thick borders.

Do NOT use neon outlines.

Do NOT create glowing UI panels.

The edge treatment must feel physical and elegant.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
17. GLASS REFRACTION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use:

• subtle refraction
• slight displacement
• gentle light bending
• controlled transparency variation

The distortion must remain extremely subtle.

Never distort:

• product packaging
• logos
• important Arabic typography
• important product information
• faces
• important objects

The purpose is to create physical realism, not visual chaos.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
18. BACKGROUND
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a sophisticated atmospheric background designed specifically to support Glassmorphism.

Prefer:

• deep black
• soft gray
• cool neutral tones
• subtle brand colors
• muted gradients
• atmospheric lighting
• soft luminous zones

The background should contain enough tonal variation for the glass surfaces to be visible.

However, it must remain visually quiet.

Avoid complicated scenery.

Avoid realistic gyms unless explicitly requested.

Avoid excessive objects.

Avoid dramatic environments.

The background exists primarily to create depth behind the glass.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
19. LIGHTING

• glass
• background
• translucent surfaces

• subtle reflections
• gentle rim lighting
• realistic contact shadows
• controlled light falloff
• soft atmospheric illumination

Do NOT create excessive glow.

Do NOT use aggressive neon lighting.

Do NOT make everything luminous.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
20. PRODUCT LIGHTING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use professional product lighting.

The product must have:

• realistic highlights
• realistic shadows
• accurate material response
• dimensional form
• sharp edges
• realistic contact with the environment

The product should appear physically present inside the Glassmorphism environment.

BACKGROUND

DISTANT GLASS
↓
MIDGROUND GLASS
↓
PRODUCT
↓
FOREGROUND GLASS ACCENTS

ARABIC TYPOGRAPHY

• creating depth
• separating information

Do NOT create a dashboard.

Do NOT make the design look like a website UI.

This is a COMMERCIAL ADVERTISEMENT, not an application interface.

27 غ بروتين

109 سعرة حرارية

86% بروتين

1 كغ

Maximum visual information should remain concise and premium.
