Does the composition feel expensive?

Would a real premium fitness or nutrition brand publish this?

If removing an element makes the composition stronger, REMOVE IT.

The final design must feel:

GLASSY.
TRANSLUCENT.
PREMIUM.
FUTURISTIC.
CLEAN.
ELEGANT.
MINIMAL.
DIMENSIONAL.
SOPHISTICATED.
ARABIC-FIRST.
COMMERCIAL.
EASY ON THE EYES.

The goal is NOT to demonstrate how many Glassmorphism effects can be added.

The goal is to use Glassmorphism with enough restraint that the product feels elevated by the environment.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
35. FINAL OUTPUT
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Generate ONE finished advertisement.

Do not generate multiple variations.

Do not show sketches.

Do not show wireframes.

Do not provide explanations.

Analyze the uploaded product image first.

Extract the reliable product information.

Select the most valuable information.

Determine the appropriate Arabic copy.

Design the composition using the specified Glassmorphism art direction.

Then generate the final polished commercial artwork directly.

The final visible advertisement should be primarily Arabic.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
36. ASPECT RATIO — CHANGE ONLY THIS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

FINAL ASPECT RATIO:

9:16 VERTICAL PORTRAIT

Design the entire composition specifically for this aspect ratio from the beginning.

Do NOT create another aspect ratio and crop it afterward.

Do NOT stretch, squeeze, or distort the composition.

All visual elements must be intentionally positioned for the specified vertical format.

Maintain safe margins around the product, Arabic typography, logo, nutritional callouts, and all important elements.

The final artwork must be a true 9:16 vertical composition optimized for Instagram Stories, Reels, and vertical social-media presentation.

prompts.title: Neumorphism / Soft UI En
prompts.promptText:
Create a premium commercial FITNESS / NUTRITION advertisement using a STRICT, SOPHISTICATED, HIGH-END NEUMORPHISM / SOFT UI DESIGN STYLE.

The final artwork must be designed specifically for an ENGLISH-SPEAKING AUDIENCE.

English must be the PRIMARY visual language of the final advertisement.

The entire composition must follow a natural LEFT-TO-RIGHT (LTR) visual and typographic flow.

The final artwork must look like it was created by an elite commercial art director, premium fitness brand designer, professional product photographer, and high-end Soft UI / Neumorphism designer working together.

The result must feel:

SOFT.
PREMIUM.
CLEAN.
TACTILE.
MODERN.
ELEGANT.
REFINED.
CALM.
DIMENSIONAL.
SOPHISTICATED.
COMMERCIAL.
EASY ON THE EYES.

This is NOT a generic "soft shadow" poster.

Do NOT simply add large shadows around random objects.

Create a genuine, professionally art-directed Neumorphism / Soft UI composition based on soft surfaces, subtle elevation, controlled light direction, gentle extrusions, recessed elements, tactile depth, restrained contrast, and physical visual consistency.

The PRODUCT remains the HERO.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1. PRODUCT INPUT
   ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

PRODUCT IMAGE:

[INSERT PRODUCT IMAGE]

The uploaded product image is the PRIMARY SOURCE OF TRUTH.

The image must be analyzed before creating the advertisement.

Do NOT require the user to manually provide product information if it can be reliably extracted from the uploaded image.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
2. PRODUCT IMAGE ANALYSIS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Before designing the advertisement, carefully inspect the uploaded product image.

Identify and extract ONLY information that is clearly visible and reliably readable from the product packaging.

Analyze:

• Product name
• Product type
• Brand name
• Flavor
• Net weight
• Serving size
• Protein amount per serving
• Calories per serving
• Protein percentage
• Carbohydrates
• Fat
• Ingredients
• Key nutritional information
• Product features
• Product claims
• Certifications
• Any other clearly printed product information

The uploaded packaging is the authoritative source.

Do NOT invent, assume, estimate, infer, or fabricate product information.

If information is partially visible but cannot be read with confidence, DO NOT use it.

If information is completely absent from the image, DO NOT create it.

If nutritional information is visible, preserve the exact values and units shown on the packaging.

Do not convert, reinterpret, round, or modify numerical values unless explicitly requested.

For example:

If the package says "27g Protein", use:

"27g Protein"

If it says "109 kcal", use:

"109 kcal"

If it says "1 KG", use:

"1 KG"

Do not change these factual values.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
3. INFORMATION SELECTION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

After analyzing the product image, automatically determine which extracted information is most valuable for a premium Soft UI commercial advertisement.

Prioritize:

1. Product name
2. Brand name
3. Most important nutritional value
4. Key product specification
5. Net weight
6. Flavor, if relevant
7. One or two important product features

Do NOT attempt to display every piece of information extracted from the packaging.

This is a PREMIUM ADVERTISEMENT, not a nutrition facts sheet.

Select only the information that improves the advertisement.

Use concise visual callouts instead of paragraphs.

For example, if clearly visible on the package:

27g Protein
109 kcal
86% Protein
1 KG

may be presented as elegant Soft UI information highlights.

Only use these values if they are actually visible and readable in the uploaded image.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
4. PRODUCT TITLE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Automatically determine the product title from the uploaded packaging.

Use the exact recognizable product name printed on the package whenever possible.

Do NOT invent a new product name.

Do NOT rewrite the brand or product name unnecessarily.

If the product title is clearly written in English, preserve it accurately.

If the product title contains a generic descriptive phrase that can be naturally presented in English, use the clearest recognizable wording.

If the product title is unclear, use only the clearly readable portion.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
5. BRAND IDENTIFICATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Automatically identify the brand from the packaging if clearly visible.

Preserve the original logo and brand identity.

Do NOT redesign the logo.

Do NOT recreate a fake logo.

Do NOT invent brand elements.

The brand should remain visually consistent with the original packaging.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
6. PRODUCT PRESERVATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use the provided product image as the PRIMARY VISUAL SOURCE.

The product is the central visual hero of the entire composition.

Do NOT unnecessarily redesign, deform, replace, recolor, or alter the product packaging.

Preserve:

• exact product shape
• packaging structure
• logo
• brand identity
• printed typography
• label details
• proportions
• colors
• recognizable characteristics
• material appearance

The product must remain immediately recognizable as the exact original product.

If the provided image contains multiple products, preserve the correct number of products.

Do not duplicate products unnecessarily.

Do not generate additional flavors, variants, containers, packages, or accessories unless they are visibly present in the uploaded image.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
7. TEXT GENERATION RULES
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The advertisement may use TWO primary sources of text:

SOURCE A — USER-PROVIDED TEXT

If the user explicitly provides promotional text, CTA, price, offer, slogan, or campaign message, it may be incorporated into the design.

SOURCE B — PRODUCT-PACKAGING INFORMATION

The AI may extract factual product information directly from the uploaded packaging.

This includes clearly readable:

• Product name
• Brand name
• Nutritional values
• Product specifications
• Flavor
• Weight
• Product features
• Printed claims

ONLY use information that is clearly supported by the uploaded image or explicitly provided by the user.

All newly generated marketing text must be written in NATURAL, PROFESSIONAL ENGLISH.

The copy must feel premium, concise, modern, and commercially appropriate.

Do NOT invent:

• nutritional facts
• ingredients
• calories
• protein percentages
• health claims
• medical claims
• prices
• discounts
• certifications
• awards
• statistics
• testimonials
• product specifications
• performance claims

Do not create marketing claims that are not supported by the packaging or user-provided information.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
8. FACTUAL ACCURACY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

This is CRITICAL.

Every factual product statement in the advertisement must be traceable to either:

1. The uploaded product packaging

OR

2. Information explicitly provided by the user.

Never fill missing information with assumptions.

Never use generic supplement statistics.

Never invent benefits simply because the product belongs to a particular category.

For example:

Do NOT automatically claim:

"Builds muscle"

"Burns fat"

"Boosts testosterone"

"Improves recovery"

"Clinically proven"

"100% pure"

"Zero sugar"

"High absorption"

unless the claim is explicitly visible on the packaging or explicitly provided by the user.

Accuracy is more important than adding more text.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
9. LANGUAGE HANDLING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The FINAL ADVERTISEMENT must be ENGLISH-FIRST.

All newly generated:

• headlines
• subtitles
• promotional messages
• CTAs
• supporting text
• product information callouts
• descriptive text

must be written in professional English.

Use NATURAL MODERN ENGLISH suitable for commercial fitness and nutrition advertising.

Use correct:

• spelling
• grammar
• punctuation
• capitalization
• typography
• LTR direction
• text hierarchy

Do NOT generate pseudo-English text.

Do NOT generate meaningless text.

Do NOT reverse text.

Do NOT mirror letters incorrectly.

All English text must read naturally from LEFT TO RIGHT.

The visual composition must also respect LTR reading flow.

Do NOT introduce unnecessary bilingual text.

English should remain the dominant language throughout the advertisement.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
10. MINIMAL SOFT-UI COPY STYLE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use short, sophisticated, premium English advertising language.

The copy should feel:

• modern
• confident
• concise
• natural
• professional
• premium
• performance-oriented

Avoid:

• cheap advertising language
• exaggerated claims
• long sentences
• unnecessary slogans
• excessive punctuation
• excessive exclamation marks
• generic motivational clichés

Prefer concise commercial language.

Examples of STYLE only:

"Built for Performance"

"Power Your Performance"

"Performance Starts Here"

"Made for Your Next Level"

"Precision in Every Serving"

These are examples of tone and structure only.

Do NOT automatically use these phrases unless they are appropriate to the specific product.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
11. CORE NEUMORPHISM / SOFT UI DIRECTION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a sophisticated PREMIUM NEUMORPHIC / SOFT UI visual system.

The design must feel tactile and physically coherent.

Use the visual principles of:

• soft extrusion
• soft elevation
• recessed surfaces
• subtle embossing
• subtle debossing
• diffuse shadows
• soft highlights
• gentle surface transitions
• controlled depth
• tactile interaction
• restrained contrast

The design should create the impression that the interface and supporting graphic elements are physically molded from the same soft material.

Use a consistent lighting direction throughout the composition.

Every raised element should appear raised.

Every recessed element should appear recessed.

Do NOT mix contradictory shadow directions.

Do NOT use hard drop shadows.

Do NOT use random 3D effects.

The visual system must feel physically consistent.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
12. PRODUCT PRIORITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The product MUST remain more visually important than every Soft UI element.

Soft UI is the supporting visual system.

The product must remain:

• sharp
• recognizable
• readable
• visually dominant
• physically grounded

Do not convert the actual product into a soft UI object.

Do not soften or blur the product.

Do not cover important packaging details with excessive shadows or embossed elements.

The product must maintain its real-world appearance.

Soft UI should create an environment around the product.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
13. VISUAL HIERARCHY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Establish a strict visual hierarchy:

1. PRODUCT
2. PRODUCT TITLE / PRIMARY MESSAGE
3. KEY PRODUCT INFORMATION
4. BRAND
5. SUPPORTING INFORMATION
6. CTA, if provided

The product must immediately attract attention.

Typography must remain secondary to the product.

Soft UI elements must remain supportive.

Decorative elements must remain subtle.

The viewer should understand the advertisement within approximately one second.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
14. SOFT SURFACE SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a unified soft surface environment.

The main background and supporting UI elements should feel like they belong to the same physical material system.

Use:

• smooth matte surfaces
• soft tonal transitions
• subtle raised surfaces
• subtle recessed surfaces
• gentle ambient shadows
• soft directional highlights

Avoid highly reflective surfaces.

Avoid metallic surfaces.

Avoid glossy plastic.

Avoid glass.

Avoid strong specular reflections.

Neumorphism should feel soft, matte, tactile, and calm.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
15. RAISED ELEMENTS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use raised Soft UI elements sparingly.

Possible uses:

• product information cards
• subtle CTA buttons
• small statistic controls
• brand containers
• decorative structural elements
• small interface-inspired labels

Raised elements should have:

• soft outer shadow
• subtle highlight on the opposite edge
• gentle elevation
• rounded geometry
• consistent depth

Do NOT create exaggerated floating cards.

Do NOT create thick 3D extrusions.

Do NOT make every element raised.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
16. RECESSED ELEMENTS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use recessed or inset surfaces selectively.

Possible uses:

• nutritional information
• small labels
• product specifications
• subtle containers
• background details

Recessed elements should feel pressed into the surface rather than placed on top of it.

Use:

• inner shadow
• soft tonal depression
• subtle edge transition
• consistent light direction

Do NOT create deep holes.

Do NOT create dramatic bevels.

The effect should remain subtle and premium.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
17. SHADOW SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use a highly controlled shadow system.

Shadows must be:

• soft
• diffuse
• realistic
• low contrast
• consistent
• physically believable

Use a consistent light source.

Every raised object should cast a believable soft shadow.

Every recessed object should use an appropriate inner shadow.

Avoid:

• hard black shadows
• multiple conflicting light sources
• exaggerated long shadows
• excessive blur
• floating-object appearance

The shadow system is one of the most important elements of the Soft UI aesthetic.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
18. HIGHLIGHT SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use extremely subtle highlights to define raised surfaces.

Highlights should be:

• soft
• restrained
• directional
• low contrast
• physically believable

Use highlights primarily along surfaces facing the main light source.

Do NOT create glowing edges.

Do NOT use neon outlines.

Do NOT use bright white borders.

The highlight should be perceived as light interacting with a soft surface.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
19. BACKGROUND
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a calm, premium background suitable for Neumorphism.

Prefer:

• warm off-white
• soft ivory
• light gray
• cool gray
• muted beige
• refined charcoal
• deep neutral tones

Choose the background based on the product packaging and brand identity.

The background should have enough tonal consistency for the Soft UI effects to remain visible.

Avoid complicated scenery.

Avoid realistic gyms unless explicitly requested.

Avoid excessive environmental objects.

Avoid dramatic backgrounds.

Avoid strong gradients.

If a gradient is used, keep it extremely subtle.

The background should feel like a continuous physical surface.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
20. PRODUCT PRESENTATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Treat the product as a premium commercial product-photography subject.

Present it with:

• realistic scale
• precise positioning
• realistic perspective
• controlled lighting
• subtle contact shadow
• clean surroundings
• professional separation

The product may be:

• centered
• slightly off-center
• aligned to a grid
• positioned using the rule of thirds
• placed within a sophisticated editorial composition

Choose the strongest placement automatically.

Do not follow a rigid template.

The product must feel intentionally staged within the Soft UI environment.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
21. PRODUCT LIGHTING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use premium commercial product photography lighting.

The product must have:

• realistic highlights
• realistic shadows
• accurate material response
• dimensional form
• sharp edges
• realistic contact with the environment

The product should feel physically present within the scene.

Do NOT apply exaggerated Neumorphic shadows directly to the product packaging.

Do NOT make the product look like a molded plastic UI component.

Keep the product realistic.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
22. DEPTH AND DIMENSION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create subtle physical depth.

Use:

• soft elevation
• recessed details
• realistic contact shadows
• subtle tonal separation
• controlled perspective
• restrained layering

Depth should feel tactile rather than cinematic.

Avoid dramatic 3D effects.

Avoid floating objects.

Avoid excessive extrusion.

The goal is a premium tactile interface-inspired advertisement, not a 3D render showcase.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
23. INFORMATION CALLOUTS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

When reliable nutritional or product information has been extracted from the packaging, present only the most important values as elegant Soft UI callouts.

Examples:

27g PROTEIN

109 KCAL

86% PROTEIN

1 KG

These are ONLY examples of formatting.

Do not automatically use these numbers unless they are actually visible on the uploaded product packaging.

Information may be placed inside:

• subtle raised surfaces
• recessed surfaces
• soft inset panels
• tactile labels

Use clean, minimal typography.

Do not turn the advertisement into an infographic.

Do not create a dashboard.

Do not display too many numbers.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
24. DISTRACTION CONTROL
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

THIS IS CRITICAL.

Neumorphism can easily become repetitive and visually muddy.

Avoid that.

The advertisement must remain extremely easy on the eyes.

DO NOT add:

• excessive raised cards
• excessive recessed elements
• dozens of buttons
• fake interface controls
• random switches
• random sliders
• unnecessary icons
• random floating objects
• excessive shadows
• excessive highlights
• excessive bevels
• hard outlines
• neon effects
• glowing surfaces
• random gym equipment
• random dumbbells
• random weights
• bodybuilding silhouettes
• unrelated athletes
• smoke
• fire
• explosions
• lightning
• excessive particles
• fake statistics
• fake product claims
• fake certifications
• visual clutter

Do not make the design look like a mobile application screen.

If an element does not improve the product presentation, REMOVE IT.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
25. COLOR SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Build the color system around the actual product packaging.

Extract the dominant visual colors from the product.

Use a restrained palette.

Prefer:

• one dominant surface color
• product colors
• one neutral supporting color
• one subtle accent

The background and Soft UI surfaces should generally remain within the same tonal family.

Do not introduce unrelated colors.

If the product packaging is highly colorful, simplify the environment.

The product should provide most of the visual color.

Avoid rainbow gradients.

Avoid excessive multicolor effects.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
26. TYPOGRAPHY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use premium modern English typography.

Typography should be:

• clean
• minimal
• sophisticated
• highly readable
• balanced
• contemporary

Use no more than TWO typefaces.

Prefer:

• modern sans-serif
• neo-grotesk
• geometric sans-serif
• clean editorial typography

All typography must follow LEFT-TO-RIGHT (LTR) direction.

Use:

• clear hierarchy
• appropriate font weights
• comfortable line height
• restrained letter spacing
• precise alignment
• consistent spacing

Typography should visually integrate with the Soft UI system without becoming embossed or overly decorative.

Do NOT use:

• decorative fonts
• childish fonts
• excessive outlines
• glowing text
• metallic text
• extreme gradients
• excessive shadows
• excessive text effects

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
27. TEXT DENSITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Keep the amount of text LOW.

This is a premium commercial advertisement, NOT a product catalog, nutrition label, or flyer.

Do not copy the entire back label into the design.

Do not display every ingredient or nutritional value.

Select only the strongest, most useful information.

Prioritize:

• visual impact
• immediate comprehension
• product recognition
• readability
• premium presentation

Use short labels and concise information.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
28. FITNESS / NUTRITION VISUAL LANGUAGE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Communicate fitness through sophisticated tactile design.

Possible concepts:

• performance
• precision
• discipline
• wellness
• strength
• recovery
• clean energy
• modern technology
• premium sports culture

Neumorphism should reinforce a sense of:

TACTILE PERFORMANCE.

Do not automatically add gym equipment.

Do not automatically add athletes.

Do not use bodybuilding clichés unless explicitly requested.

The product itself should communicate the fitness or nutrition category whenever possible.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
29. NEGATIVE SPACE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Maintain generous breathing room.

Soft UI requires controlled negative space.

Do not fill empty areas with additional raised or recessed elements.

Empty space should create:

• elegance
• focus
• clarity
• visual breathing room
• premium perception

The design should feel spacious rather than crowded.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
30. COMPOSITION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use professional commercial composition.

Possible approaches:

• central hero
• asymmetric editorial composition
• rule-of-thirds
• vertical product emphasis
• tactile layered composition
• controlled diagonal flow
• grid-based composition

Choose the strongest composition automatically based on the product image and extracted information.

Do not mechanically follow a template.

The composition must feel custom-designed for the specific product.

Maintain a consistent LTR visual flow.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
31. GRID AND ALIGNMENT
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use an invisible professional grid.

Maintain:

• consistent margins
• consistent spacing
• alignment between text elements
• proportional relationships
• disciplined placement
• visual rhythm

Product, typography, logo, and Soft UI information elements should feel connected through alignment.

Avoid randomly positioned elements.

Do not create excessive columns.

Keep the structure simple.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
32. BRANDING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

If a brand name or logo is clearly visible on the product:

Integrate it subtly and professionally.

Do not overpower the product.

Do not redesign the logo.

Do not recreate a fake logo.

Do not invent brand elements.

Maintain visual consistency with the original packaging.

The brand should feel like part of the composition rather than an additional sticker.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
33. PREMIUM COMMERCIAL QUALITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The final advertisement should feel suitable for:

• premium sports nutrition brands
• luxury fitness brands
• modern wellness companies
• high-end supplement companies
• athletic technology brands
• professional commercial campaigns
• premium social-media advertising

Think:

LUXURY FITNESS BRANDING

*

PREMIUM SPORTS NUTRITION

*

HIGH-END NEUMORPHISM

*

SOFT UI ART DIRECTION

*

COMMERCIAL PRODUCT PHOTOGRAPHY

Do NOT make it look like:

• a generic AI poster
• a cheap supplement advertisement
• a mobile app screen
• a UI mockup
• a dashboard
• a gaming poster
• a futuristic sci-fi poster
• a bodybuilding poster
• a crowded Instagram template
• a generic Canva design

The design should feel sophisticated and timeless.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
34. IMAGE QUALITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Prioritize extremely high visual quality.

The final artwork must have:

• photorealistic product presentation
• accurate packaging
• realistic materials
• physically believable Soft UI surfaces
• realistic shadows
• realistic highlights
• consistent lighting direction
• clean edges
• sharp product details
• sophisticated depth
• professional color grading
• premium art direction
• polished English typography
• commercial-quality finish

Avoid:

• warped packaging
• distorted logos
• duplicated products
• malformed objects
• unreadable text
• inconsistent shadow direction
• hard artificial shadows
• excessive bevels
• fake 3D surfaces
• plastic-looking UI elements
• unrealistic lighting
• inconsistent perspective
• AI artifacts
• invented product information

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
35. FINAL ART-DIRECTION CHECK
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Before finalizing the artwork, evaluate it as a professional commercial Neumorphism / Soft UI art director.

Ask:

Is the product immediately recognizable?

Is the product the strongest visual element?

Did the product analysis use only information actually visible in the uploaded image?

Are all nutritional values and specifications accurate?

Did the design avoid invented claims?

Is all newly generated text in natural, correct English?

Does the typography follow proper LTR composition?

Does the Neumorphism feel physically believable?

Is the light direction consistent?

Do raised elements actually look raised?

Do recessed elements actually look recessed?

Are the shadows soft and controlled?

Are the highlights subtle?

Does the Soft UI system support the product rather than compete with it?

Is there enough negative space?

Are there too many interface-like elements?

Does the design look like an advertisement rather than an application interface?

Does the product feel premium?

Does the design feel tactile?

Does the composition feel expensive?

Would a real premium fitness or nutrition brand publish this?

If removing an element makes the composition stronger, REMOVE IT.

The final design must feel:

SOFT.
TACTILE.
PREMIUM.
CLEAN.
MODERN.
ELEGANT.
REFINED.
DIMENSIONAL.
CALM.
SOPHISTICATED.
COMMERCIAL.
EASY ON THE EYES.

The goal is NOT to demonstrate how many Neumorphic effects can be added.

The goal is to use Soft UI with enough restraint that the product feels elevated by a tactile, premium environment.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
36. FINAL OUTPUT
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Generate ONE finished advertisement.

Do not generate multiple variations.

Do not show sketches.

Do not show wireframes.

Do not provide explanations.

Analyze the uploaded product image first.

Extract the reliable product information.

Select the most valuable information.

Determine the appropriate English copy.

Design the composition using the specified Neumorphism / Soft UI art direction.

Then generate the final polished commercial artwork directly.

The final visible advertisement should be primarily English and follow a strict LTR visual structure.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
37. ASPECT RATIO — CHANGE ONLY THIS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

FINAL ASPECT RATIO:

9:16 VERTICAL PORTRAIT

Design the entire composition specifically for this aspect ratio from the beginning.

Do NOT create another aspect ratio and crop it afterward.

Do NOT stretch, squeeze, or distort the composition.

All visual elements must be intentionally positioned for the specified vertical format.

Maintain safe margins around the product, English typography, logo, nutritional callouts, and all important elements.

The final artwork must be a true 9:16 vertical composition optimized for Instagram Stories, Reels, and vertical social-media presentation.

prompts.title: Neumorphism / Soft UI Ar
prompts.promptText:
Create a premium commercial FITNESS / NUTRITION advertisement using a STRICT, SOPHISTICATED, HIGH-END NEUMORPHISM / SOFT UI DESIGN STYLE.

The final artwork must be designed specifically for an ARABIC-SPEAKING AUDIENCE.

Arabic must be the PRIMARY visual language of the final advertisement.

The entire composition must follow a natural RIGHT-TO-LEFT (RTL) visual and typographic flow.

The final artwork must look like it was created by an elite commercial art director, premium fitness brand designer, professional product photographer, Arabic typography specialist, and high-end Neumorphism / Soft UI designer working together.

The result must feel:

SOFT.
PREMIUM.
CLEAN.
TACTILE.
MODERN.
ELEGANT.
REFINED.
CALM.
DIMENSIONAL.
SOPHISTICATED.
COMMERCIAL.
ARABIC-FIRST.
EASY ON THE EYES.

This is NOT a generic "soft shadow" poster.

Do NOT simply add large shadows around random objects.

Create a genuine, professionally art-directed Neumorphism / Soft UI composition based on soft surfaces, subtle elevation, gentle extrusions, recessed elements, tactile depth, restrained contrast, consistent lighting, and physically coherent visual relationships.

The PRODUCT remains the HERO.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1. PRODUCT INPUT
   ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

PRODUCT IMAGE:

[INSERT PRODUCT IMAGE]

The uploaded product image is the PRIMARY SOURCE OF TRUTH.

The image must be analyzed before creating the advertisement.

Do NOT require the user to manually provide product information if it can be reliably extracted from the uploaded image.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
2. PRODUCT IMAGE ANALYSIS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Before designing the advertisement, carefully inspect the uploaded product image.

Identify and extract ONLY information that is clearly visible and reliably readable from the product packaging.

Analyze:

• اسم المنتج
• نوع المنتج
• اسم العلامة التجارية
• النكهة
• الوزن الصافي
• حجم الحصة
• كمية البروتين في الحصة
• السعرات الحرارية في الحصة
• نسبة البروتين
• الكربوهيدرات
• الدهون
• المكونات
• المعلومات الغذائية الأساسية
• خصائص المنتج
• ادعاءات المنتج
• الشهادات
• أي معلومات أخرى مطبوعة بوضوح على العبوة

The uploaded packaging is the authoritative source.

Do NOT invent, assume, estimate, infer, or fabricate product information.

If information is partially visible but cannot be read with confidence, DO NOT use it.

If information is completely absent from the image, DO NOT create it.

If nutritional information is visible, preserve the exact factual values and units shown on the packaging.

Do not convert, reinterpret, round, or modify numerical values unless explicitly requested.

For example:

If the package says:

"27g Protein"

the Arabic advertisement may present it as:

"27 غ بروتين"

If it says:

"109 kcal"

it may be presented as:

"109 سعرة حرارية"

If it says:

"1 KG"

it may be presented as:

"1 كغ"

The factual numerical value must remain unchanged.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
3. INFORMATION SELECTION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

After analyzing the product image, automatically determine which extracted information is most valuable for a premium Soft UI commercial advertisement.

Prioritize:

1. اسم المنتج
2. اسم العلامة التجارية
3. أهم قيمة غذائية
4. أهم مواصفة للمنتج
5. الوزن الصافي
6. النكهة، إذا كانت مهمة
7. خاصية أو خاصيتان مهمتان للمنتج

Do NOT attempt to display every piece of information extracted from the packaging.

This is a PREMIUM ADVERTISEMENT, not a nutrition facts sheet.

Select only the information that improves the advertisement.

Use concise Arabic visual callouts instead of paragraphs.

For example, if clearly visible on the package:

27g Protein
109 kcal
86% Protein
1 KG

may be presented as:

27 غ بروتين
109 سعرة حرارية
86% بروتين
1 كغ

Only use these values if they are actually visible and readable in the uploaded image.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
4. PRODUCT TITLE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Automatically determine the product title from the uploaded packaging.

Use the exact recognizable product name printed on the package whenever possible.

Do NOT invent a new product name.

Do NOT unnecessarily rewrite the brand or product name.

If the official product name is in English or another language, preserve the official product name when appropriate.

If a generic descriptive phrase can be naturally translated into Arabic without changing the product identity, translate it professionally.

Do NOT translate official brand names.

If the product title is unclear, use only the clearly readable portion.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
5. BRAND IDENTIFICATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Automatically identify the brand from the packaging if clearly visible.

Preserve the original logo and brand identity.

Do NOT redesign the logo.

Do NOT recreate a fake logo.

Do NOT invent brand elements.

Do NOT translate the official brand name unless explicitly requested.

The brand should remain visually consistent with the original packaging.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
6. PRODUCT PRESERVATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use the provided product image as the PRIMARY VISUAL SOURCE.

The product is the central visual hero of the entire composition.

Do NOT unnecessarily redesign, deform, replace, recolor, or alter the product packaging.

Preserve:

• exact product shape
• packaging structure
• logo
• brand identity
• printed typography
• label details
• proportions
• colors
• recognizable characteristics
• material appearance

The product must remain immediately recognizable as the exact original product.

If the provided image contains multiple products, preserve the correct number of products.

Do not duplicate products unnecessarily.

Do not generate additional flavors, variants, containers, packages, or accessories unless they are visibly present in the uploaded image.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
7. TEXT GENERATION RULES
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The advertisement may use TWO primary sources of text:

SOURCE A — USER-PROVIDED TEXT

If the user explicitly provides promotional text, CTA, price, offer, slogan, or campaign message, it may be incorporated into the design.

If the user-provided promotional text is in English but the final advertisement is intended for an Arabic-speaking audience, translate it naturally into professional Arabic unless the user explicitly requests English.

SOURCE B — PRODUCT-PACKAGING INFORMATION

The AI may extract factual product information directly from the uploaded packaging.

This includes clearly readable:

• اسم المنتج
• اسم العلامة التجارية
• القيم الغذائية
• مواصفات المنتج
• النكهة
• الوزن
• خصائص المنتج
• الادعاءات المطبوعة

ONLY use information that is clearly supported by the uploaded image or explicitly provided by the user.

All newly generated marketing text must be written in NATURAL, PROFESSIONAL, CORRECT ARABIC.

The copy must feel premium, concise, modern, and commercially appropriate.

Do NOT invent:

• nutritional facts
• ingredients
• calories
• protein percentages
• health claims
• medical claims
• prices
• discounts
• certifications
• awards
• statistics
• testimonials
• product specifications
• performance claims

Do not create marketing claims that are not supported by the packaging or user-provided information.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
8. FACTUAL ACCURACY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

This is CRITICAL.

Every factual product statement in the advertisement must be traceable to either:

1. The uploaded product packaging

OR

2. Information explicitly provided by the user.

Never fill missing information with assumptions.

Never use generic supplement statistics.

Never invent benefits simply because the product belongs to a particular category.

For example:

Do NOT automatically claim:

"يساعد على بناء العضلات"

"يحرق الدهون"

"يعزز هرمون التستوستيرون"

"يحسن الاستشفاء"

"مثبت سريريًا"

"نقي 100%"

"خالي من السكر"

"امتصاص سريع"

unless the claim is explicitly visible on the packaging or explicitly provided by the user.

Accuracy is more important than adding more text.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
9. LANGUAGE HANDLING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The FINAL ADVERTISEMENT must be ARABIC-FIRST.

All newly generated:

• headlines
• subtitles
• promotional messages
• CTAs
• supporting text
• product information callouts
• descriptive text

must be written in professional Arabic.

Use NATURAL MODERN ARABIC suitable for commercial fitness and nutrition advertising.

Use correct:

• spelling
• grammar
• punctuation
• Arabic typography
• RTL direction
• text hierarchy
• Arabic letter connections

Do NOT generate pseudo-Arabic text.

Do NOT generate meaningless Arabic-like text.

Do NOT reverse Arabic text.

Do NOT mirror Arabic letters incorrectly.

All Arabic text must read naturally from RIGHT TO LEFT.

The visual composition must also respect RTL reading flow.

The viewer's eye should naturally move through the design according to Arabic visual reading direction.

Do NOT introduce unnecessary bilingual text.

English should only remain when it is part of:

• the original product packaging
• the official brand identity
• the official product name
• a user-provided element that the user explicitly wants preserved

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
10. ARABIC SOFT-UI COPY STYLE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use short, sophisticated, premium Arabic advertising language.

The copy should feel:

• modern
• confident
• concise
• natural
• professional
• premium
• performance-oriented

Avoid:

• cheap advertising language
• exaggerated claims
• long sentences
• unnecessary slogans
• excessive punctuation
• excessive exclamation marks
• generic motivational clichés

Prefer concise commercial Arabic.

Examples of STYLE only:

"أداء أقوى يبدأ من هنا"

"طاقة تدعم أداءك"

"اختيارك للأداء الأفضل"

"مصمم لأداءك اليومي"

"قوة في كل جرعة"

These are examples of tone and structure only.

Do NOT automatically use these phrases unless they are appropriate to the specific product.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
11. CORE NEUMORPHISM / SOFT UI DIRECTION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a sophisticated PREMIUM NEUMORPHIC / SOFT UI visual system.

The design must feel tactile and physically coherent.

Use the visual principles of:

• soft extrusion
• soft elevation
• recessed surfaces
• subtle embossing
• subtle debossing
• diffuse shadows
• soft highlights
• gentle surface transitions
• controlled depth
• tactile interaction
• restrained contrast

The design should create the impression that the interface and supporting graphic elements are physically molded from the same soft material.

Use a consistent lighting direction throughout the composition.

Every raised element should appear raised.

Every recessed element should appear recessed.

Do NOT mix contradictory shadow directions.

Do NOT use hard drop shadows.

Do NOT use random 3D effects.

The visual system must feel physically consistent.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
12. PRODUCT PRIORITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The product MUST remain more visually important than every Soft UI element.

Soft UI is the supporting visual system.

The product must remain:

• sharp
• recognizable
• readable
• visually dominant
• physically grounded

Do not convert the actual product into a Soft UI object.

Do not soften or blur the product.

Do not cover important packaging details with excessive shadows or embossed elements.

The product must maintain its real-world appearance.

Soft UI should create an environment around the product.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
13. VISUAL HIERARCHY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Establish a strict visual hierarchy:

1. PRODUCT
2. ARABIC PRODUCT TITLE / PRIMARY MESSAGE
3. KEY PRODUCT INFORMATION
4. BRAND
5. SUPPORTING INFORMATION
6. CTA, if provided

The product must immediately attract attention.

Arabic typography must remain secondary to the product.

Soft UI elements must remain supportive.

Decorative elements must remain subtle.

The viewer should understand the advertisement within approximately one second.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
14. SOFT SURFACE SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a unified soft surface environment.

The main background and supporting UI elements should feel like they belong to the same physical material system.

Use:

• smooth matte surfaces
• soft tonal transitions
• subtle raised surfaces
• subtle recessed surfaces
• gentle ambient shadows
• soft directional highlights

Avoid highly reflective surfaces.

Avoid metallic surfaces.

Avoid glossy plastic.

Avoid glass.

Avoid strong specular reflections.

Neumorphism should feel soft, matte, tactile, and calm.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
15. RAISED ELEMENTS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use raised Soft UI elements sparingly.

Possible uses:

• product information cards
• subtle CTA buttons
• small statistic controls
• brand containers
• decorative structural elements
• small interface-inspired labels

Raised elements should have:

• soft outer shadow
• subtle highlight on the opposite edge
• gentle elevation
• rounded geometry
• consistent depth

Do NOT create exaggerated floating cards.

Do NOT create thick 3D extrusions.

Do NOT make every element raised.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
16. RECESSED ELEMENTS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use recessed or inset surfaces selectively.

Possible uses:

• nutritional information
• small labels
• product specifications
• subtle containers
• background details

Recessed elements should feel pressed into the surface rather than placed on top of it.

Use:

• inner shadow
• soft tonal depression
• subtle edge transition
• consistent light direction

Do NOT create deep holes.

Do NOT create dramatic bevels.

The effect should remain subtle and premium.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
17. SHADOW SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use a highly controlled shadow system.

Shadows must be:

• soft
• diffuse
• realistic
• low contrast
• consistent
• physically believable

Use a consistent light source.

Every raised object should cast a believable soft shadow.

Every recessed object should use an appropriate inner shadow.

Avoid:

• hard black shadows
• multiple conflicting light sources
• exaggerated long shadows
• excessive blur
• floating-object appearance

The shadow system is one of the most important elements of the Soft UI aesthetic.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
18. HIGHLIGHT SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use extremely subtle highlights to define raised surfaces.

Highlights should be:

• soft
• restrained
• directional
• low contrast
• physically believable

Use highlights primarily along surfaces facing the main light source.

Do NOT create glowing edges.

Do NOT use neon outlines.

Do NOT use bright white borders.

The highlight should be perceived as light interacting with a soft surface.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
19. BACKGROUND
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a calm, premium background suitable for Neumorphism.

Prefer:

• warm off-white
• soft ivory
• light gray
• cool gray
• muted beige
• refined charcoal
• deep neutral tones

Choose the background based on the product packaging and brand identity.

The background should have enough tonal consistency for the Soft UI effects to remain visible.

Avoid complicated scenery.

Avoid realistic gyms unless explicitly requested.

Avoid excessive environmental objects.

Avoid dramatic backgrounds.

Avoid strong gradients.

If a gradient is used, keep it extremely subtle.

The background should feel like a continuous physical surface.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
20. PRODUCT PRESENTATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Treat the product as a premium commercial product-photography subject.

Present it with:

• realistic scale
• precise positioning
• realistic perspective
• controlled lighting
• subtle contact shadow
• clean surroundings
• professional separation

The product may be:

• centered
• slightly off-center
• aligned to a grid
• positioned using the rule of thirds
• placed within a sophisticated editorial composition

Choose the strongest placement automatically.

Do not follow a rigid template.

The product must feel intentionally staged within the Soft UI environment.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
21. PRODUCT LIGHTING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use premium commercial product photography lighting.

The product must have:

• realistic highlights
• realistic shadows
• accurate material response
• dimensional form
• sharp edges
• realistic contact with the environment

The product should feel physically present within the scene.

Do NOT apply exaggerated Neumorphic shadows directly to the product packaging.

Do NOT make the product look like a molded plastic UI component.

Keep the product realistic.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
22. DEPTH AND DIMENSION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create subtle physical depth.

Use:

• soft elevation
• recessed details
• realistic contact shadows
• subtle tonal separation
• controlled perspective
• restrained layering

Depth should feel tactile rather than cinematic.

Avoid dramatic 3D effects.

Avoid floating objects.

Avoid excessive extrusion.

The goal is a premium tactile interface-inspired advertisement, not a 3D render showcase.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
23. INFORMATION CALLOUTS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

When reliable nutritional or product information has been extracted from the packaging, present only the most important values as elegant Soft UI callouts.

Examples:

27 غ بروتين

109 سعرة حرارية

86% بروتين

1 كغ

These are ONLY examples of formatting.

Do not automatically use these numbers unless they are actually visible on the uploaded product packaging.

Information may be placed inside:

• subtle raised surfaces
• recessed surfaces
• soft inset panels
• tactile labels

Use clean, minimal Arabic typography.

Do not turn the advertisement into an infographic.

Do not create a dashboard.

Do not display too many numbers.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
24. DISTRACTION CONTROL
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

THIS IS CRITICAL.

Neumorphism can easily become repetitive and visually muddy.

Avoid that.

The advertisement must remain extremely easy on the eyes.

DO NOT add:

• excessive raised cards
• excessive recessed elements
• dozens of buttons
• fake interface controls
• random switches
• random sliders
• unnecessary icons
• random floating objects
• excessive shadows
• excessive highlights
• excessive bevels
• hard outlines
• neon effects
• glowing surfaces
• random gym equipment
• random dumbbells
• random weights
• bodybuilding silhouettes
• unrelated athletes
• smoke
• fire
• explosions
• lightning
• excessive particles
• fake statistics
• fake product claims
• fake certifications
• visual clutter

Do not make the design look like a mobile application screen.

If an element does not improve the product presentation, REMOVE IT.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
25. COLOR SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Build the color system around the actual product packaging.

Extract the dominant visual colors from the product.

Use a restrained palette.

Prefer:

• one dominant surface color
• product colors
• one neutral supporting color
• one subtle accent

The background and Soft UI surfaces should generally remain within the same tonal family.

Do not introduce unrelated colors.

If the product packaging is highly colorful, simplify the environment.

The product should provide most of the visual color.

Avoid rainbow gradients.

Avoid excessive multicolor effects.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
26. ARABIC TYPOGRAPHY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use premium modern Arabic typography.

Typography should be:

• clean
• minimal
• sophisticated
• highly readable
• balanced
• contemporary

Prefer professional Arabic sans-serif typography such as:

• Cairo
• IBM Plex Sans Arabic
• DIN Next Arabic style
• modern geometric Arabic sans-serif
• clean contemporary Arabic typography

Use no more than TWO typefaces.

All Arabic typography must follow RIGHT-TO-LEFT direction.

Use:

• appropriate Arabic font weight
• comfortable line height
• balanced spacing
• proper RTL alignment
• strong contrast
• clear hierarchy
• generous breathing room

Typography should visually integrate with the Soft UI system without becoming embossed or overly decorative.

Do NOT use:

• decorative Arabic fonts
• childish fonts
• excessive calligraphy
• distorted Arabic letters
• incorrect letter connections
• reversed text
• excessive outlines
• glowing Arabic text
• metallic Arabic text
• excessive text effects

Arabic typography must look professionally typeset.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
27. TEXT DENSITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Keep the amount of text LOW.

This is a premium commercial advertisement, NOT a product catalog, nutrition label, or flyer.

Do not copy the entire back label into the design.

Do not display every ingredient or nutritional value.

Select only the strongest, most useful information.

Prioritize:

• visual impact
• immediate comprehension
• product recognition
• readability
• premium presentation

Use short Arabic labels and concise information.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
28. FITNESS / NUTRITION VISUAL LANGUAGE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Communicate fitness through sophisticated tactile design.

Possible concepts:

• performance
• precision
• discipline
• wellness
• strength
• recovery
• clean energy
• modern technology
• premium sports culture

Neumorphism should reinforce a sense of:

TACTILE PERFORMANCE.

Do not automatically add gym equipment.

Do not automatically add athletes.

Do not use bodybuilding clichés unless explicitly requested.

The product itself should communicate the fitness or nutrition category whenever possible.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
29. NEGATIVE SPACE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Maintain generous breathing room.

Soft UI requires controlled negative space.

Do not fill empty areas with additional raised or recessed elements.

Empty space should create:

• elegance
• focus
• clarity
• visual breathing room
• premium perception

The design should feel spacious rather than crowded.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
30. COMPOSITION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use professional commercial composition.

Possible approaches:

• central hero
• asymmetric editorial composition
• rule-of-thirds
• vertical product emphasis
• tactile layered composition
• controlled diagonal flow
• grid-based composition

Choose the strongest composition automatically based on the product image and extracted information.

Do not mechanically follow a template.

The composition must feel custom-designed for the specific product.

Maintain a consistent RTL visual flow.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
31. GRID AND ALIGNMENT
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use an invisible professional grid.

Maintain:

• consistent margins
• consistent spacing
• alignment between Arabic text elements
• proportional relationships
• disciplined placement
• visual rhythm

Product, Arabic typography, logo, and Soft UI information elements should feel connected through alignment.

Avoid randomly positioned elements.

Do not create excessive columns.

Keep the structure simple.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
32. BRANDING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

If a brand name or logo is clearly visible on the product:

Integrate it subtly and professionally.

Do not overpower the product.

Do not redesign the logo.

Do not recreate a fake logo.

Do not invent brand elements.

Do not translate the official brand name unless explicitly requested.

Maintain visual consistency with the original packaging.

The brand should feel like part of the composition rather than an additional sticker.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
33. PREMIUM COMMERCIAL QUALITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The final advertisement should feel suitable for:

• premium sports nutrition brands
• luxury fitness brands
• modern wellness companies
• high-end supplement companies
• athletic technology brands
• professional commercial campaigns
• premium Arabic social-media advertising

Think:

LUXURY FITNESS BRANDING

*

PREMIUM SPORTS NUTRITION

*

HIGH-END NEUMORPHISM

*

SOFT UI ART DIRECTION

*

ARABIC COMMERCIAL ART DIRECTION

*

COMMERCIAL PRODUCT PHOTOGRAPHY

Do NOT make it look like:

• a generic AI poster
• a cheap supplement advertisement
• a mobile app screen
• a UI mockup
• a dashboard
• a gaming poster
• a futuristic sci-fi poster
• a bodybuilding poster
• a crowded Instagram template
• a generic Canva design

The design should feel sophisticated and timeless.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
34. IMAGE QUALITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Prioritize extremely high visual quality.

The final artwork must have:

• photorealistic product presentation
• accurate packaging
• realistic materials
• physically believable Soft UI surfaces
• realistic shadows
• realistic highlights
• consistent lighting direction
• clean edges
• sharp product details
• sophisticated depth
• professional color grading
• premium art direction
• polished Arabic typography
• commercial-quality finish

Avoid:

• warped packaging
• distorted logos
• duplicated products
• malformed objects
• unreadable Arabic text
• incorrect Arabic typography
• inconsistent shadow direction
• hard artificial shadows
• excessive bevels
• fake 3D surfaces
• plastic-looking UI elements
• unrealistic lighting
• inconsistent perspective
• AI artifacts
• invented product information

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
35. FINAL ART-DIRECTION CHECK
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Before finalizing the artwork, evaluate it as a professional Arabic commercial Neumorphism / Soft UI art director.

Ask:

Is the product immediately recognizable?

Is the product the strongest visual element?

Did the product analysis use only information actually visible in the uploaded image?

Are all nutritional values and specifications accurate?

Did the design avoid invented claims?

Is all newly generated text in natural, correct Arabic?

Does the typography follow proper RTL composition?

Is the Arabic typography professionally typeset?

Does the Neumorphism feel physically believable?

Is the light direction consistent?

Do raised elements actually look raised?

Do recessed elements actually look recessed?

Are the shadows soft and controlled?

Are the highlights subtle?

Does the Soft UI system support the product rather than compete with it?

Is there enough negative space?

Are there too many interface-like elements?

Does the design look like an advertisement rather than an application interface?

Does the product feel premium?

Does the design feel tactile?

Does the composition feel expensive?

Would a real premium fitness or nutrition brand publish this?

If removing an element makes the composition stronger, REMOVE IT.

The final design must feel:

SOFT.
TACTILE.
PREMIUM.
CLEAN.
MODERN.
ELEGANT.
REFINED.
DIMENSIONAL.
CALM.
SOPHISTICATED.
ARABIC-FIRST.
COMMERCIAL.
EASY ON THE EYES.

The goal is NOT to demonstrate how many Neumorphic effects can be added.

The goal is to use Soft UI with enough restraint that the product feels elevated by a tactile, premium environment.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
36. FINAL OUTPUT
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Generate ONE finished advertisement.

Do not generate multiple variations.

Do not show sketches.

Do not show wireframes.

Do not provide explanations.

Analyze the uploaded product image first.

Extract the reliable product information.

Select the most valuable information.

Determine the appropriate Arabic copy.

Design the composition using the specified Neumorphism / Soft UI art direction.

Then generate the final polished commercial artwork directly.

The final visible advertisement should be primarily Arabic and follow a strict RTL visual structure.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
37. ASPECT RATIO — CHANGE ONLY THIS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

FINAL ASPECT RATIO:

9:16 VERTICAL PORTRAIT

Design the entire composition specifically for this aspect ratio from the beginning.

Do NOT create another aspect ratio and crop it afterward.

Do NOT stretch, squeeze, or distort the composition.

All visual elements must be intentionally positioned for the specified vertical format.

Maintain safe margins around the product, Arabic typography, logo, nutritional callouts, and all important elements.

The final artwork must be a true 9:16 vertical composition optimized for Instagram Stories, Reels, and vertical social-media presentation.

prompts.title: Skeuomorphism En
prompts.promptText:
Create a premium commercial FITNESS / NUTRITION advertisement using a STRICT, SOPHISTICATED, HIGH-END SKEUOMORPHISM DESIGN STYLE.

The final artwork must be designed specifically for an ENGLISH-SPEAKING AUDIENCE.

English must be the PRIMARY visual language of the final advertisement.

The entire composition must follow a natural LEFT-TO-RIGHT (LTR) visual and typographic flow.

The final artwork must look like it was created by an elite commercial art director, premium fitness brand designer, professional product photographer, tactile product designer, and high-end Skeuomorphic visual designer working together.

The result must feel:

TACTILE.
REALISTIC.
PREMIUM.
PHYSICAL.
AUTHENTIC.
CRAFTED.
REFINED.
DETAILED.
MODERN.
SOPHISTICATED.
COMMERCIAL.
EASY ON THE EYES.

This is NOT a generic "realistic poster."

Do NOT simply add textures, shadows, and 3D objects randomly.

Create a genuine, professionally art-directed Skeuomorphic composition where digital graphic elements visually behave like real physical materials and objects.

The design should create the impression that the viewer could physically touch, press, open, lift, slide, emboss, peel, or interact with the visual elements.

The PRODUCT remains the HERO.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1. PRODUCT INPUT
   ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

PRODUCT IMAGE:

[INSERT PRODUCT IMAGE]

The uploaded product image is the PRIMARY SOURCE OF TRUTH.

The image must be analyzed before creating the advertisement.

Do NOT require the user to manually provide product information if it can be reliably extracted from the uploaded image.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
2. PRODUCT IMAGE ANALYSIS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Before designing the advertisement, carefully inspect the uploaded product image.

Identify and extract ONLY information that is clearly visible and reliably readable from the product packaging.

Analyze:

• Product name
• Product type
• Brand name
• Flavor
• Net weight
• Serving size
• Protein amount per serving
• Calories per serving
• Protein percentage
• Carbohydrates
• Fat
• Ingredients
• Key nutritional information
• Product features
• Product claims
• Certifications
• Any other clearly printed product information

The uploaded packaging is the authoritative source.

Do NOT invent, assume, estimate, infer, or fabricate product information.

If information is partially visible but cannot be read with confidence, DO NOT use it.

If information is completely absent from the image, DO NOT create it.

If nutritional information is visible, preserve the exact values and units shown on the packaging.

Do not convert, reinterpret, round, or modify numerical values unless explicitly requested.

For example:

If the package says "27g Protein", use:

"27g Protein"

If it says "109 kcal", use:

"109 kcal"

If it says "1 KG", use:

"1 KG"

Do not change these factual values.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
3. INFORMATION SELECTION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

After analyzing the product image, automatically determine which extracted information is most valuable for a premium Skeuomorphic commercial advertisement.

Prioritize:

1. Product name
2. Brand name
3. Most important nutritional value
4. Key product specification
5. Net weight
6. Flavor, if relevant
7. One or two important product features

Do NOT attempt to display every piece of information extracted from the packaging.

This is a PREMIUM ADVERTISEMENT, not a nutrition facts sheet.

Select only the information that improves the advertisement.

Use concise physical-looking information labels, tags, plaques, cards, or panels instead of paragraphs.

Only use nutritional values and specifications that are actually visible and readable in the uploaded image.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
4. PRODUCT TITLE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Automatically determine the product title from the uploaded packaging.

Use the exact recognizable product name printed on the package whenever possible.

Do NOT invent a new product name.

Do NOT rewrite the brand or product name unnecessarily.

If the product title is clearly written in English, preserve it accurately.

If the product title contains a generic descriptive phrase that can be naturally presented in English, use the clearest recognizable wording.

If the product title is unclear, use only the clearly readable portion.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
5. BRAND IDENTIFICATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Automatically identify the brand from the packaging if clearly visible.

Preserve the original logo and brand identity.

Do NOT redesign the logo.

Do NOT recreate a fake logo.

Do NOT invent brand elements.

The brand should remain visually consistent with the original packaging.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
6. PRODUCT PRESERVATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use the provided product image as the PRIMARY VISUAL SOURCE.

The product is the central visual hero of the entire composition.

Do NOT unnecessarily redesign, deform, replace, recolor, or alter the product packaging.

Preserve:

• exact product shape
• packaging structure
• logo
• brand identity
• printed typography
• label details
• proportions
• colors
• recognizable characteristics
• material appearance

The product must remain immediately recognizable as the exact original product.

If the provided image contains multiple products, preserve the correct number of products.

Do not duplicate products unnecessarily.

Do not generate additional flavors, variants, containers, packages, or accessories unless they are visibly present in the uploaded image.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
7. TEXT GENERATION RULES
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The advertisement may use TWO primary sources of text:

SOURCE A — USER-PROVIDED TEXT

If the user explicitly provides promotional text, CTA, price, offer, slogan, or campaign message, it may be incorporated into the design.

SOURCE B — PRODUCT-PACKAGING INFORMATION

The AI may extract factual product information directly from the uploaded packaging.

This includes clearly readable:

• Product name
• Brand name
• Nutritional values
• Product specifications
• Flavor
• Weight
• Product features
• Printed claims

ONLY use information that is clearly supported by the uploaded image or explicitly provided by the user.

All newly generated marketing text must be written in NATURAL, PROFESSIONAL ENGLISH.

The copy must feel premium, concise, modern, and commercially appropriate.

Do NOT invent:

• nutritional facts
• ingredients
• calories
• protein percentages
• health claims
• medical claims
• prices
• discounts
• certifications
• awards
• statistics
• testimonials
• product specifications
• performance claims

Do not create marketing claims that are not supported by the packaging or user-provided information.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
8. FACTUAL ACCURACY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

This is CRITICAL.

Every factual product statement in the advertisement must be traceable to either:

1. The uploaded product packaging

OR

2. Information explicitly provided by the user.

Never fill missing information with assumptions.

Never use generic supplement statistics.

Never invent benefits simply because the product belongs to a particular category.

For example:

Do NOT automatically claim:

"Builds muscle"

"Burns fat"

"Boosts testosterone"

"Improves recovery"

"Clinically proven"

"100% pure"

"Zero sugar"

"High absorption"

unless the claim is explicitly visible on the packaging or explicitly provided by the user.

Accuracy is more important than adding more text.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
9. LANGUAGE HANDLING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The FINAL ADVERTISEMENT must be ENGLISH-FIRST.

All newly generated:

• headlines
• subtitles
• promotional messages
• CTAs
• supporting text
• product information callouts
• descriptive text

must be written in professional English.

Use NATURAL MODERN ENGLISH suitable for commercial fitness and nutrition advertising.

Use correct:

• spelling
• grammar
• punctuation
• capitalization
• typography
• LTR direction
• text hierarchy

Do NOT generate pseudo-English text.

Do NOT generate meaningless text.

Do NOT reverse text.

Do NOT mirror letters incorrectly.

All English text must read naturally from LEFT TO RIGHT.

The visual composition must also respect LTR reading flow.

Do NOT introduce unnecessary bilingual text.

English should remain the dominant language throughout the advertisement.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
10. SKEUOMORPHIC COPY STYLE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use short, sophisticated, premium English advertising language.

The copy should feel:

• modern
• confident
• concise
• natural
• professional
• premium
• performance-oriented

Avoid:

• cheap advertising language
• exaggerated claims
• long sentences
• unnecessary slogans
• excessive punctuation
• excessive exclamation marks
• generic motivational clichés

Prefer concise commercial language.

Examples of STYLE only:

"Built for Performance"

"Power Your Performance"

"Performance Starts Here"

"Precision in Every Serving"

"Made for Your Next Level"

These are examples of tone and structure only.

Do NOT automatically use these phrases unless they are appropriate to the specific product.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
11. CORE SKEUOMORPHISM DIRECTION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a sophisticated PREMIUM SKEUOMORPHIC visual system.

The fundamental principle is:

DIGITAL GRAPHIC ELEMENTS SHOULD LOOK AND BEHAVE LIKE REAL PHYSICAL OBJECTS.

Use realistic physical metaphors such as:

• leather
• paper
• brushed metal
• polished metal
• rubber
• molded plastic
• fabric
• canvas
• wood
• cardboard
• embossed surfaces
• stitched surfaces
• printed labels
• physical tags
• engraved plates
• tactile buttons
• physical switches
• realistic cards
• textured surfaces

Choose materials according to the product and brand.

Do NOT use every material simultaneously.

Select a coherent material language.

Every physical element must appear to belong to the same real-world environment.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
12. PRODUCT PRIORITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The product MUST remain more visually important than every Skeuomorphic element.

The physical environment is the supporting visual system.

The product must remain:

• sharp
• recognizable
• readable
• visually dominant
• physically grounded

Do not hide the product behind decorative objects.

Do not cover important packaging details.

Do not transform the actual product into an unrelated physical object.

The product itself must remain authentic.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
13. VISUAL HIERARCHY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Establish a strict visual hierarchy:

1. PRODUCT
2. PRODUCT TITLE / PRIMARY MESSAGE
3. KEY PRODUCT INFORMATION
4. BRAND
5. SUPPORTING INFORMATION
6. CTA, if provided

The product must immediately attract attention.

Typography must remain secondary to the product.

Physical decorative elements must remain supportive.

The viewer should understand the advertisement within approximately one second.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
14. MATERIAL SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a coherent physical material system.

Select only materials that complement the product.

Possible combinations include:

• matte paper + embossed ink
• dark leather + metallic details
• brushed aluminum + rubber
• premium cardboard + printed labels
• textured fabric + stitched patches
• molded matte plastic + engraved controls

Materials must have realistic:

• texture
• roughness
• reflectivity
• imperfections
• edge behavior
• light response
• depth

Avoid generic CGI materials.

Avoid overly perfect surfaces.

Real materials should have subtle physical imperfections.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
15. EMBOSSING AND DEBOSSING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use physical print techniques where appropriate.

Possible treatments:

• embossed logo
• debossed title
• raised lettering
• pressed typography
• engraved information
• stamped marks
• foil-like physical details

These effects must appear physically integrated into the material.

Do NOT simply add a drop shadow behind text.

The viewer should believe the typography is physically printed, pressed, stamped, or engraved.

Keep these effects restrained.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
16. PHYSICAL LABELS AND TAGS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use physical-looking information elements when appropriate.

Possible forms:

• paper labels
• hanging tags
• adhesive labels
• metal plaques
• stitched patches
• printed cards
• embossed badges
• small physical specification plates

These elements may contain verified product information.

They must feel physically attached to the environment.

Use realistic:

• attachment
• folds
• thickness
• edges
• shadows
• material interaction

Do NOT create random decorative labels.

Every label must communicate something useful.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
17. PHYSICAL CONTROLS AND INTERACTION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

If interface-inspired elements are used, they must appear physically real.

Possible elements:

• tactile buttons
• rotary dials
• switches
• sliders
• knobs
• mechanical indicators
• physical toggles

Use them very sparingly.

They should support the advertising concept rather than make the design look like a dashboard.

Do NOT create a fake application interface.

Do NOT fill the design with unnecessary controls.

Every control must have a clear visual or conceptual purpose.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
18. SHADOW SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use realistic physical shadows.

Shadows should communicate:

• object height
• contact
• thickness
• depth
• physical placement

Use:

• contact shadows
• cast shadows
• ambient occlusion
• subtle directional shadows

Maintain a consistent light source.

Objects must not appear to float unless intentionally suspended.

Avoid:

• hard artificial shadows
• inconsistent shadow directions
• excessive black shadows
• excessive blur
• fake floating objects

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
19. HIGHLIGHT AND REFLECTION SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use realistic material-specific highlights.

Metal should behave like metal.

Plastic should behave like plastic.

Leather should behave like leather.

Paper should remain mostly matte.

Rubber should remain soft and low-reflective.

Glass, if used, should behave like real glass.

Do not use the same reflection style on every material.

The light response must reinforce the physical identity of each surface.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
20. BACKGROUND
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a sophisticated physical environment that supports the product.

Possible environments include:

• premium studio tabletop
• textured paper surface
• matte stone
• brushed metal surface
• refined leather surface
• clean wooden surface
• premium fabric surface
• minimal industrial surface

Choose the environment according to the product.

Keep the environment restrained.

Do NOT create an overly elaborate scene.

Do NOT automatically place the product inside a gym.

Do NOT add unrelated fitness equipment.

The background should establish physical context without competing with the product.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
21. PRODUCT PRESENTATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Treat the product as a premium real-world commercial product.

Present it with:

• realistic scale
• accurate perspective
• natural contact with the surface
• realistic weight
• believable placement
• physically accurate shadows
• professional lighting

The product may be:

• centered
• slightly off-center
• aligned to a grid
• positioned using the rule of thirds
• placed within a tactile editorial composition

Choose the strongest placement automatically.

The product must feel physically present rather than digitally pasted into the scene.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
22. PRODUCT LIGHTING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use premium commercial product photography lighting.

The product must have:

• realistic highlights
• realistic shadows
• accurate material response
• dimensional form
• sharp edges
• realistic contact with the environment

Lighting should reveal both the product and the physical environment.

Do NOT over-light the scene.

Do NOT create dramatic cinematic lighting unless it genuinely improves the product.

Maintain realistic material response.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
23. DEPTH AND PHYSICALITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create convincing physical depth.

Use:

• object thickness
• layered materials
• realistic edges
• contact shadows
• cast shadows
• subtle perspective
• physical overlap
• material interaction
• realistic scale

Objects should feel like they occupy real space.

Do not make everything perfectly flat.

Do not make everything dramatically 3D.

The physical depth should feel natural.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
24. INFORMATION CALLOUTS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

When reliable nutritional or product information has been extracted from the packaging, present only the most important values as physical-looking information elements.

Examples:

27g PROTEIN

109 KCAL

86% PROTEIN

1 KG

These are ONLY examples of formatting.

Do not automatically use these numbers unless they are actually visible on the uploaded product packaging.

Information may be presented as:

• embossed labels
• printed paper cards
• engraved metal plates
• stitched patches
• physical tags
• stamped labels
• tactile specification panels

Choose the format that best fits the material language.

Do not turn the advertisement into an infographic.

Do not display too many numbers.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
25. DISTRACTION CONTROL
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

THIS IS CRITICAL.

Skeuomorphism can easily become overloaded with textures and objects.

Avoid that.

The advertisement must remain extremely easy on the eyes.

DO NOT add:

• random physical objects
• unnecessary buttons
• random switches
• excessive labels
• excessive badges
• random gym equipment
• random dumbbells
• random weights
• bodybuilding silhouettes
• unrelated athletes
• random ingredients
• excessive textures
• excessive stitching
• excessive metallic objects
• excessive leather
• excessive wood
• excessive paper
• excessive reflections
• excessive shadows
• smoke
• fire
• explosions
• lightning
• excessive particles
• fake statistics
• fake product claims
• fake certifications
• visual clutter

Do NOT make the advertisement look like a collection of unrelated objects.

Every physical element must have a clear purpose.

If an element does not improve the product presentation, REMOVE IT.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
26. COLOR SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Build the color system around the actual product packaging.

Extract the dominant visual colors from the product.

Use a restrained physical color palette.

Prefer:

• one dominant environmental tone
• product colors
• one material tone
• one subtle accent

Choose material colors that complement the product.

Avoid unrelated colors.

Avoid excessive saturation.

Avoid rainbow effects.

The physical materials should support the product's existing brand identity rather than compete with it.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
27. TYPOGRAPHY

Use premium modern English typography.

Typography should be:

• clean
• sophisticated
• highly readable
• balanced
• contemporary
• physically integrated

Use no more than TWO typefaces.

Prefer:

• modern sans-serif
• refined grotesk
• editorial sans-serif
• premium condensed sans-serif where appropriate

All typography must follow LEFT-TO-RIGHT (LTR) direction.

Typography may visually behave like a physical material:

• printed ink
• embossed lettering
• debossed lettering
• engraved text
• stamped typography
• foil-like physical print

However, readability always comes first.

Do NOT use:

• decorative fonts
• childish fonts
• excessive calligraphy
• unreadable vintage fonts
• excessive outlines
• glowing text
• neon text
• excessive gradients
• excessive text effects

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
28. TEXT DENSITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Keep the amount of text LOW.

This is a premium commercial advertisement, NOT a product catalog, nutrition label, or flyer.

Do not copy the entire back label into the design.

Do not display every ingredient or nutritional value.

Select only the strongest, most useful information.

Prioritize:

• visual impact
• immediate comprehension
• product recognition
• readability
• tactile presentation
• premium perception

Use short labels and concise information.

Possible concepts:

• performance
• strength
• craftsmanship
• precision
• discipline
• durability
• wellness
• recovery

Skeuomorphism should reinforce a sense of:

REAL-WORLD PERFORMANCE.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
30. NEGATIVE SPACE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

• visual breathing room

Do not make the scene feel like a tabletop covered with objects.

31. COMPOSITION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use professional commercial composition.

Possible approaches:

• central hero
• asymmetric editorial composition
• rule-of-thirds
• product-led tabletop composition
• tactile layered composition
• controlled diagonal flow
• grid-based composition

Choose the strongest composition automatically based on the product image and extracted information.

Do not mechanically follow a template.

The composition must feel custom-designed for the specific product.

Maintain a consistent LTR visual flow.

• consistent margins
• consistent spacing
• alignment between text elements
• proportional relationships
• disciplined placement
• visual rhythm

Avoid randomly positioned objects.

Do not create excessive columns.

Keep the structure simple.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
36. FINAL ART-DIRECTION CHECK
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Before finalizing the artwork, evaluate it as a professional commercial Skeuomorphic art director.

Ask:

Is the product immediately recognizable?

Is the product the strongest visual element?

Did the product analysis use only information actually visible in the uploaded image?

Are all nutritional values and specifications accurate?

Did the design avoid invented claims?

Is all newly generated text in natural, correct English?

Does the typography follow proper LTR composition?

Do the physical materials look believable?

Does each material behave according to its physical properties?

Do the shadows communicate real object placement?

Are the reflections appropriate for each material?

Do objects have believable thickness?

Does the environment feel physically coherent?
