The goal is NOT to demonstrate how many graphic shapes can be added.

The goal is to communicate the product with maximum visual clarity using the minimum number of necessary visual elements.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
32. FINAL OUTPUT
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Generate ONE finished advertisement.

Do not generate multiple variations.

Do not show sketches.

Do not show wireframes.

Do not provide explanations.

Analyze the uploaded product image first.

Extract the reliable product information.

Select the most valuable information.

Determine the appropriate Arabic copy.

Design the composition using the specified Flat Design art direction.

Then generate the final polished commercial artwork directly.

The final visible advertisement should be primarily Arabic and follow a strict RTL visual structure.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
33. ASPECT RATIO — CHANGE ONLY THIS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

FINAL ASPECT RATIO:

9:16 VERTICAL PORTRAIT

Design the entire composition specifically for this aspect ratio from the beginning.

Do NOT create another aspect ratio and crop it afterward.

Do NOT stretch, squeeze, or distort the composition.

All visual elements must be intentionally positioned for the specified vertical format.

Maintain safe margins around the product, Arabic typography, logo, icons, information blocks, and all important elements.

The final artwork must be a true 9:16 vertical composition optimized for Instagram Stories, Reels, and vertical social-media presentation.

prompts.title: Material Design En
prompts.promptText:
Create a premium commercial FITNESS / NUTRITION advertisement using a STRICT, SOPHISTICATED, HIGH-END MATERIAL DESIGN STYLE.

The final artwork must be designed specifically for an ENGLISH-SPEAKING AUDIENCE.

English must be the PRIMARY visual language of the final advertisement.

The entire composition must follow a natural LEFT-TO-RIGHT (LTR) visual and typographic flow.

The final artwork must look like it was created by an elite commercial art director, premium fitness brand designer, professional product photographer, Material Design specialist, typography specialist, and high-end visual communication designer working together.

The result must feel:

MODERN.
CLEAN.
STRUCTURED.
PREMIUM.
FUNCTIONAL.
CONFIDENT.
POLISHED.
INTUITIVE.
DIMENSIONAL.
BALANCED.
COMMERCIAL.
EASY ON THE EYES.

This is NOT a generic "Google-style poster."

Do NOT simply add cards, shadows, and bright colors.

Create a genuine, professionally art-directed Material Design composition based on clear hierarchy, purposeful surfaces, elevation, meaningful motion-inspired geometry, bold typography, restrained depth, systematic spacing, and highly intentional visual organization.

The PRODUCT remains the HERO.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1. PRODUCT INPUT
   ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

PRODUCT IMAGE:

[INSERT PRODUCT IMAGE]

The uploaded product image is the PRIMARY SOURCE OF TRUTH.

The image must be analyzed before creating the advertisement.

Do NOT require the user to manually provide product information if it can be reliably extracted from the uploaded image.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
2. PRODUCT IMAGE ANALYSIS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Before designing the advertisement, carefully inspect the uploaded product image.

Identify and extract ONLY information that is clearly visible and reliably readable from the product packaging.

Analyze:

• Product name
• Product type
• Brand name
• Flavor
• Net weight
• Serving size
• Protein amount per serving
• Calories per serving
• Protein percentage
• Carbohydrates
• Fat
• Ingredients
• Key nutritional information
• Product features
• Product claims
• Certifications
• Any other clearly printed product information

The uploaded packaging is the authoritative source.

Do NOT invent, assume, estimate, infer, or fabricate product information.

If information is partially visible but cannot be read with confidence, DO NOT use it.

If information is completely absent from the image, DO NOT create it.

If nutritional information is visible, preserve the exact factual values and units shown on the packaging.

Do not convert, reinterpret, round, or modify numerical values unless explicitly requested.

For example:

If the package says:

"27g Protein"

use:

"27g Protein"

If it says:

"109 kcal"

use:

"109 kcal"

If it says:

"1 KG"

use:

"1 KG"

The factual numerical value must remain unchanged.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
3. INFORMATION SELECTION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

After analyzing the product image, automatically determine which extracted information is most valuable for a premium Material Design commercial advertisement.

Prioritize:

1. Product name
2. Brand name
3. Most important nutritional value
4. Key product specification
5. Net weight
6. Flavor, if relevant
7. One or two important product features

Do NOT attempt to display every piece of information extracted from the packaging.

This is a PREMIUM ADVERTISEMENT, not a nutrition facts sheet.

Select only the information that improves the advertisement.

Use concise English visual callouts instead of paragraphs.

Only use nutritional values and specifications that are actually visible and readable in the uploaded image.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
4. PRODUCT TITLE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Automatically determine the product title from the uploaded packaging.

Use the exact recognizable product name printed on the packaging whenever possible.

Do NOT invent a new product name.

Do NOT unnecessarily rewrite the brand or product name.

If the official product name is clearly written in English, preserve it accurately.

If a generic descriptive phrase can be naturally presented in English without changing the product identity, use professional wording.

If the product title is unclear, use only the clearly readable portion.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
5. BRAND IDENTIFICATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Automatically identify the brand from the packaging if clearly visible.

Preserve the original logo and brand identity.

Do NOT redesign the logo.

Do NOT recreate a fake logo.

Do NOT invent brand elements.

The brand should remain visually consistent with the original packaging.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
6. PRODUCT PRESERVATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use the provided product image as the PRIMARY VISUAL SOURCE.

The product is the central visual hero of the entire composition.

Do NOT unnecessarily redesign, deform, replace, recolor, or alter the product packaging.

Preserve:

• exact product shape
• packaging structure
• logo
• brand identity
• printed typography
• label details
• proportions
• colors
• recognizable characteristics
• material appearance

The product must remain immediately recognizable as the exact original product.

If the provided image contains multiple products, preserve the correct number of products.

Do not duplicate products unnecessarily.

Do not generate additional flavors, variants, containers, packages, or accessories unless they are visibly present in the uploaded image.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
7. TEXT GENERATION RULES
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The advertisement may use TWO primary sources of text:

SOURCE A — USER-PROVIDED TEXT

If the user explicitly provides promotional text, CTA, price, offer, slogan, or campaign message, it may be incorporated into the design.

SOURCE B — PRODUCT-PACKAGING INFORMATION

The AI may extract factual product information directly from the uploaded packaging.

This includes clearly readable:

• Product name
• Brand name
• Nutritional values
• Product specifications
• Flavor
• Weight
• Product features
• Printed claims

ONLY use information that is clearly supported by the uploaded image or explicitly provided by the user.

All newly generated marketing text must be written in NATURAL, PROFESSIONAL ENGLISH.

The copy must feel premium, concise, modern, and commercially appropriate.

Do NOT invent:

• nutritional facts
• ingredients
• calories
• protein percentages
• health claims
• medical claims
• prices
• discounts
• certifications
• awards
• statistics
• testimonials
• product specifications
• performance claims

Do not create marketing claims that are not supported by the packaging or user-provided information.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
8. FACTUAL ACCURACY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

This is CRITICAL.

Every factual product statement in the advertisement must be traceable to either:

1. The uploaded product packaging

OR

2. Information explicitly provided by the user.

Never fill missing information with assumptions.

Never use generic supplement statistics.

Never invent benefits simply because the product belongs to a particular category.

For example:

Do NOT automatically claim:

"Builds muscle"

"Burns fat"

"Boosts testosterone"

"Improves recovery"

"Clinically proven"

"100% pure"

"Zero sugar"

"Fast absorption"

unless the claim is explicitly visible on the packaging or explicitly provided by the user.

Accuracy is more important than adding more text.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
9. LANGUAGE HANDLING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The FINAL ADVERTISEMENT must be ENGLISH-FIRST.

All newly generated:

• headlines
• subtitles
• promotional messages
• CTAs
• supporting text
• product information callouts
• descriptive text

must be written in professional English.

Use NATURAL MODERN ENGLISH suitable for commercial fitness and nutrition advertising.

Use correct:

• spelling
• grammar
• punctuation
• capitalization
• typography
• LTR direction
• text hierarchy

Do NOT generate pseudo-English text.

Do NOT generate meaningless text.

Do NOT reverse text.

Do NOT mirror letters incorrectly.

All English text must read naturally from LEFT TO RIGHT.

The visual composition must also respect LTR reading flow.

Do NOT introduce unnecessary bilingual text.

English should remain the dominant language throughout the advertisement.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
10. MATERIAL-DESIGN COPY STYLE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use short, sophisticated, premium English advertising language.

The copy should feel:

• modern
• confident
• concise
• natural
• professional
• energetic
• performance-oriented

Avoid:

• cheap advertising language
• exaggerated claims
• long sentences
• unnecessary slogans
• excessive punctuation
• excessive exclamation marks
• generic motivational clichés

Prefer concise commercial language.

Examples of STYLE only:

"Built for Performance"

"Fuel Your Performance"

"Performance Starts Here"

"Power Every Session"

"Made for Your Next Level"

These are examples of tone and structure only.

Do NOT automatically use these phrases unless they are appropriate to the specific product.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
11. CORE MATERIAL DESIGN DIRECTION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a sophisticated PREMIUM MATERIAL DESIGN visual system.

Material Design should be treated as a systematic visual language based on:

• clear surfaces
• meaningful elevation
• structured hierarchy
• consistent spacing
• bold typography
• purposeful color
• simple geometry
• controlled depth
• intuitive information organization

Use a strong visual system rather than random UI decoration.

The advertisement should feel inspired by a beautifully designed modern digital interface while remaining clearly a PREMIUM COMMERCIAL PRODUCT ADVERTISEMENT.

Do NOT make the design look like an actual mobile application screenshot.

The interface-inspired language should support the product rather than replace the advertisement.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
12. PRODUCT PRIORITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The product MUST remain more visually important than every Material Design element.

Material Design is the supporting visual system.

The product must remain:

• sharp
• recognizable
• readable
• visually dominant
• physically believable

Do NOT flatten or distort the actual product.

Do NOT turn the product packaging into a UI illustration.

Do NOT replace the product with a digital representation.

The real product image must remain the hero.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
13. VISUAL HIERARCHY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Establish a strict visual hierarchy:

1. PRODUCT
2. PRODUCT TITLE / PRIMARY MESSAGE
3. KEY PRODUCT INFORMATION
4. BRAND
5. SUPPORTING INFORMATION
6. CTA, if provided

The product must immediately attract attention.

Typography must remain secondary to the product.

UI-inspired surfaces must remain supportive.

The viewer should understand the advertisement within approximately one second.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
14. SURFACE SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a clear hierarchy of visual surfaces.

Use:

• background surface
• elevated content surfaces
• product stage
• information cards
• subtle containers
• controlled floating elements

Every surface must have a clear purpose.

Do NOT create cards simply because Material Design uses cards.

Cards should group related information or strengthen hierarchy.

Use rounded corners carefully and consistently.

Avoid excessive rounded rectangles.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
15. ELEVATION SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use a deliberate elevation hierarchy.

Possible levels:

LEVEL 0:
Background surface.

LEVEL 1:
Subtle information containers.

LEVEL 2:
Important information panels.

LEVEL 3:
Primary CTA or featured element.

LEVEL 4:
The PRODUCT as the visual hero.

Elevation must communicate hierarchy.

Use subtle shadows to separate surfaces.

Do NOT make every element appear equally elevated.

Do NOT use exaggerated floating cards.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
16. SHADOW SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use controlled Material Design-inspired shadows.

Shadows should be:

• soft
• subtle
• directional
• consistent
• purposeful

Use shadows primarily to communicate elevation and separation.

Avoid:

• heavy black shadows
• dramatic cinematic shadows
• multiple conflicting light sources
• excessive blur
• glowing edges
• floating-object overload

The product may retain realistic commercial photography shadows.

UI surfaces should use restrained elevation shadows.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
17. COLOR SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Build a disciplined Material-inspired color system around the actual product packaging.

Use:

• primary color
• secondary color
• surface color
• background color
• accent color
• neutral supporting tones

Extract the dominant visual identity from the product.

Use strong color intentionally.

Do NOT introduce unrelated colors.

Avoid rainbow palettes.

Avoid excessive gradients.

If gradients are used, they must be extremely subtle and purposeful.

The product should remain the strongest source of brand color.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
18. PRIMARY COLOR
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Select ONE dominant primary accent derived from the product packaging or brand identity.

Use it strategically for:

• key headings
• accent lines
• information emphasis
• CTA
• selected geometric elements

Do not use the primary color everywhere.

Color must communicate hierarchy.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
19. BACKGROUND
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a clean, modern Material-inspired background.

Possible approaches:

• solid neutral surface
• refined light surface
• dark Material-inspired surface
• subtle tonal background
• restrained color field

Choose the background according to the product and brand.

The background must remain visually quiet enough to support the product.

Avoid realistic environments unless explicitly requested.

Do NOT automatically create a gym scene.

Do NOT add random fitness equipment.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
20. PRODUCT PRESENTATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Treat the product as a premium commercial product-photography subject placed within a sophisticated Material Design environment.

Present it with:

• accurate scale
• realistic perspective
• precise positioning
• natural grounding
• controlled visual separation
• subtle elevation from the background when appropriate

The product may be:

• centered
• slightly off-center
• aligned to a grid
• positioned using the rule of thirds
• placed on a subtle elevated surface
• framed by Material-inspired geometry

Choose the strongest placement automatically.

The actual product must remain realistic.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
21. PRODUCT LIGHTING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use premium commercial product photography lighting.

The product must have:

• realistic highlights
• realistic shadows
• accurate material response
• dimensional form
• sharp edges
• realistic contact with the environment

Keep the UI-inspired environment visually consistent with the product lighting.

Do NOT make the product look like a flat digital sticker.

Do NOT over-light the scene.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
22. DEPTH AND DIMENSION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use depth to establish hierarchy, not spectacle.

Create subtle dimensional relationships between:

• background
• surfaces
• information panels
• product
• graphic elements

Use:

• controlled elevation
• soft shadows
• layering
• overlap
• subtle scale differences

Avoid:

• excessive 3D
• dramatic floating objects
• glassmorphism
• neumorphism
• heavy bevels
• exaggerated perspective

The style must remain distinctly Material Design.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
23. GEOMETRIC SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use simple geometric elements inspired by modern Material visual language.

Possible elements:

• circles
• rounded rectangles
• lines
• bars
• capsules
• subtle geometric panels
• simple accent shapes

Use them to:

• frame the product
• guide the eye
• organize information
• establish rhythm
• reinforce brand color

Do NOT add decorative geometry without purpose.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
24. INFORMATION CALLOUTS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

When reliable nutritional or product information has been extracted from the packaging, present only the most important values inside clean Material-inspired information surfaces.

Examples:

27g
PROTEIN

109
KCAL

86%
PROTEIN

1 KG

These are ONLY examples of formatting.

Do not automatically use these numbers unless they are actually visible on the uploaded product packaging.

Information may be presented using:

• elevated cards
• compact information panels
• clean metric blocks
• circular indicators
• minimal dividers
• structured labels

Keep them concise.

Do not create a dashboard.

Do not display too many numbers.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
25. CTA DESIGN
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

If the user provides a CTA, price, offer, or promotional action, present it as a clear Material-inspired interactive element.

Possible treatment:

• elevated button
• clean pill button
• rectangular action surface
• bold color block

The CTA must be visually important but must NOT compete with the product.

Do NOT invent a CTA if none is provided or appropriate.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
26. DISTRACTION CONTROL
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

THIS IS CRITICAL.

Material Design can easily become an unnecessary UI mockup.

Avoid that.

The advertisement must remain extremely easy on the eyes.

DO NOT add:

• random cards
• excessive cards
• fake app navigation
• fake menus
• fake tabs
• fake switches
• fake sliders
• random buttons
• random icons
• dashboards
• navigation bars
• status bars
• random gym equipment
• random dumbbells
• random weights
• bodybuilding silhouettes
• unrelated athletes
• excessive gradients
• excessive shadows
• excessive circles
• excessive UI elements
• fake statistics
• fake product claims
• fake certifications
• visual clutter

Do NOT make the design look like a mobile application.

The viewer must immediately understand that this is a PRODUCT ADVERTISEMENT.

If an element does not improve the product presentation, REMOVE IT.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
27. TYPOGRAPHY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use premium modern English typography.

Typography should be:

• clean
• bold
• highly readable
• modern
• systematic
• confident
• professionally balanced

Use no more than TWO typefaces.

Prefer:

• modern sans-serif
• geometric sans-serif
• contemporary grotesk
• clean editorial typography

Create a strong typographic hierarchy using:

• headline
• subheadline
• metric
• label
• CTA

All typography must follow LEFT-TO-RIGHT (LTR) direction.

Do NOT use:

• decorative fonts
• childish fonts
• excessive script fonts
• distorted typography
• glowing text
• metallic text
• excessive gradients
• excessive outlines
• excessive text effects

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
28. TEXT DENSITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Keep the amount of text LOW.

This is a premium commercial advertisement, NOT a product catalog, nutrition label, or application screen.

Do not copy the entire back label into the design.

Do not display every ingredient or nutritional value.

Select only the strongest, most useful information.

Prioritize:

• visual impact
• immediate comprehension
• product recognition
• readability
• structured hierarchy
• premium presentation

Use short labels and concise information.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
29. FITNESS / NUTRITION VISUAL LANGUAGE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Communicate fitness through:

• performance
• precision
• strength
• energy
• discipline
• modern technology
• wellness
• athletic lifestyle

Material Design should reinforce a sense of:

MODERN PERFORMANCE.

The visual system should feel organized, efficient, intelligent, and contemporary.

Do not automatically add gym equipment.

Do not automatically add athletes.

Do not use bodybuilding clichés unless explicitly requested.

The product itself should communicate the fitness or nutrition category whenever possible.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
30. NEGATIVE SPACE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Maintain generous and intentional negative space.

Use empty space to:

• isolate the product
• strengthen hierarchy
• improve readability
• separate surfaces
• create premium perception
• reduce visual fatigue

Do not fill empty areas with additional UI elements.

Empty space is part of the design system.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
31. COMPOSITION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use professional Material-inspired composition principles.

Possible approaches:

• centered hero
• asymmetric editorial layout
• product-focused card hierarchy
• structured grid
• rule-of-thirds
• vertical product emphasis
• layered surface composition
• strong color-accent composition

Choose the strongest composition automatically based on the product image and extracted information.

Do not mechanically follow a template.

The composition must feel custom-designed for the specific product.

Maintain a consistent LTR visual flow.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
32. GRID AND SPACING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use a disciplined spacing system.

Maintain:

• consistent margins
• consistent padding
• consistent gaps
• precise alignment
• proportional relationships
• visual rhythm

Use a clear modular grid.

Information cards should share consistent dimensions and spacing.

Do not randomly position UI-inspired elements.

The composition should feel systematic without becoming rigid.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
33. BRANDING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

If a brand name or logo is clearly visible on the product:

Integrate it subtly and professionally.

Do not overpower the product.

Do not redesign the logo.

Do not recreate a fake logo.

Do not invent brand elements.

Maintain visual consistency with the original packaging.

The brand should feel naturally integrated into the Material Design system.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
34. PREMIUM COMMERCIAL QUALITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The final advertisement should feel suitable for:

• premium sports nutrition brands
• luxury fitness brands
• modern wellness companies
• high-end supplement companies
• athletic technology brands
• premium performance brands
• professional commercial campaigns

Think:

LUXURY FITNESS BRANDING

*

PREMIUM SPORTS NUTRITION

*

HIGH-END MATERIAL DESIGN

*

MODERN DIGITAL PRODUCT DESIGN

*

COMMERCIAL PRODUCT PHOTOGRAPHY

*

EDITORIAL ART DIRECTION

Do NOT make it look like:

• a generic AI poster
• a cheap supplement advertisement
• a mobile app screenshot
• a dashboard
• a UI mockup
• a generic Google template
• a gaming poster
• a bodybuilding poster
• a crowded Instagram template
• a generic Canva design

The design should feel premium, modern, systematic, and commercially intentional.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
35. IMAGE QUALITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Prioritize extremely high visual quality.

The final artwork must have:

• photorealistic product presentation
• accurate packaging
• sharp product details
• clean UI-inspired geometry
• crisp edges
• precise typography
• accurate color relationships
• realistic product lighting
• controlled elevation
• professional composition
• polished English typography
• premium art direction
• commercial-quality finish

Avoid:

• warped packaging
• distorted logos
• duplicated products
• malformed objects
• unreadable text
• inconsistent geometry
• sloppy alignment
• excessive UI elements
• excessive shadows
• excessive gradients
• AI artifacts
• invented product information

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
36. FINAL ART-DIRECTION CHECK
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Before finalizing the artwork, evaluate it as a professional commercial Material Design art director.

Ask:

Is the product immediately recognizable?

Is the product the strongest visual element?

Did the product analysis use only information actually visible in the uploaded image?

Are all nutritional values and specifications accurate?

Did the design avoid invented claims?

Is all newly generated text in natural, correct English?

Does the typography follow proper LTR composition?

Is the visual hierarchy immediately understandable?

Does the elevation system communicate hierarchy?

Are the cards purposeful?

Are the surfaces organized?

Are the colors controlled?

Are there too many UI elements?

Does the design look like an advertisement rather than an application?

Is there enough negative space?

Does the composition feel genuinely Material Design?

Does it look premium rather than generic?

Does the product feel premium?

Does the composition feel professionally art-directed?

Would a real premium fitness or nutrition brand publish this?

If removing an element makes the composition stronger, REMOVE IT.

The final design must feel:

MODERN.
CLEAN.
STRUCTURED.
PREMIUM.
FUNCTIONAL.
CONFIDENT.
POLISHED.
INTUITIVE.
DIMENSIONAL.
BALANCED.
COMMERCIAL.
EASY ON THE EYES.

The goal is NOT to demonstrate how many UI elements can be added.

The goal is to use Material Design principles to create an exceptionally clear, structured, premium product advertisement.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
37. FINAL OUTPUT
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Generate ONE finished advertisement.

Do not generate multiple variations.

Do not show sketches.

Do not show wireframes.

Do not provide explanations.

Analyze the uploaded product image first.

Extract the reliable product information.

Select the most valuable information.

Determine the appropriate English copy.

Design the composition using the specified Material Design art direction.

Then generate the final polished commercial artwork directly.

The final visible advertisement should be primarily English and follow a strict LTR visual structure.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
38. ASPECT RATIO — CHANGE ONLY THIS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

FINAL ASPECT RATIO:

9:16 VERTICAL PORTRAIT

Design the entire composition specifically for this aspect ratio from the beginning.

Do NOT create another aspect ratio and crop it afterward.

Do NOT stretch, squeeze, or distort the composition.

All visual elements must be intentionally positioned for the specified vertical format.

Maintain safe margins around the product, English typography, logo, information cards, CTA, and all important elements.

The final artwork must be a true 9:16 vertical composition optimized for Instagram Stories, Reels, and vertical social-media presentation.

prompts.title: Material Design Ar
prompts.promptText:
Create a premium commercial FITNESS / NUTRITION advertisement using a STRICT, SOPHISTICATED, HIGH-END MATERIAL DESIGN STYLE.

The final artwork must be designed specifically for an ARABIC-SPEAKING AUDIENCE.

Arabic must be the PRIMARY visual language of the final advertisement.

The entire composition must follow a natural RIGHT-TO-LEFT (RTL) visual and typographic flow.

The final artwork must look like it was created by an elite commercial art director, premium fitness brand designer, professional product photographer, Material Design specialist, Arabic typography specialist, and high-end visual communication designer working together.

The result must feel:

MODERN.
CLEAN.
STRUCTURED.
PREMIUM.
FUNCTIONAL.
CONFIDENT.
POLISHED.
INTUITIVE.
DIMENSIONAL.
BALANCED.
ARABIC-FIRST.
COMMERCIAL.
EASY ON THE EYES.

This is NOT a generic "Google-style poster."

Do NOT simply add cards, shadows, and bright colors.

Create a genuine, professionally art-directed Material Design composition based on clear hierarchy, meaningful elevation, structured surfaces, purposeful color, systematic spacing, bold Arabic typography, simple geometry, restrained depth, and highly intentional visual organization.

The PRODUCT remains the HERO.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1. PRODUCT INPUT
   ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

PRODUCT IMAGE:

[INSERT PRODUCT IMAGE]

The uploaded product image is the PRIMARY SOURCE OF TRUTH.

The image must be analyzed before creating the advertisement.

Do NOT require the user to manually provide product information if it can be reliably extracted from the uploaded image.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
2. PRODUCT IMAGE ANALYSIS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Before designing the advertisement, carefully inspect the uploaded product image.

Identify and extract ONLY information that is clearly visible and reliably readable from the product packaging.

Analyze:

• اسم المنتج
• نوع المنتج
• اسم العلامة التجارية
• النكهة
• الوزن الصافي
• حجم الحصة
• كمية البروتين في الحصة
• السعرات الحرارية في الحصة
• نسبة البروتين
• الكربوهيدرات
• الدهون
• المكونات
• المعلومات الغذائية الأساسية
• خصائص المنتج
• ادعاءات المنتج
• الشهادات
• أي معلومات أخرى مطبوعة بوضوح على العبوة

The uploaded packaging is the authoritative source.

Do NOT invent, assume, estimate, infer, or fabricate product information.

If information is partially visible but cannot be read with confidence, DO NOT use it.

If information is completely absent from the image, DO NOT create it.

If nutritional information is visible, preserve the exact factual values and units shown on the packaging.

Do not convert, reinterpret, round, or modify numerical values unless explicitly requested.

For example:

If the package says:

"27g Protein"

the Arabic advertisement may present it as:

"27 غ بروتين"

If it says:

"109 kcal"

it may be presented as:

"109 سعرة حرارية"

If it says:

"1 KG"

it may be presented as:

"1 كغ"

The factual numerical value must remain unchanged.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
3. INFORMATION SELECTION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

After analyzing the product image, automatically determine which extracted information is most valuable for a premium Material Design commercial advertisement.

Prioritize:

1. اسم المنتج
2. اسم العلامة التجارية
3. أهم قيمة غذائية
4. أهم مواصفة للمنتج
5. الوزن الصافي
6. النكهة، إذا كانت مهمة
7. خاصية أو خاصيتان مهمتان للمنتج

Do NOT attempt to display every piece of information extracted from the packaging.

This is a PREMIUM ADVERTISEMENT, not a nutrition facts sheet.

Select only the information that improves the advertisement.

Use concise Arabic visual callouts instead of paragraphs.

Only use nutritional values and specifications that are actually visible and readable in the uploaded image.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
4. PRODUCT TITLE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Automatically determine the product title from the uploaded packaging.

Use the exact recognizable product name printed on the packaging whenever possible.

Do NOT invent a new product name.

Do NOT unnecessarily rewrite the brand or product name.

If the official product name is in English or another language, preserve the official product name when appropriate.

If a generic descriptive phrase can be naturally translated into Arabic without changing the product identity, translate it professionally.

Do NOT translate official brand names.

If the product title is unclear, use only the clearly readable portion.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
5. BRAND IDENTIFICATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Automatically identify the brand from the packaging if clearly visible.

Preserve the original logo and brand identity.

Do NOT redesign the logo.

Do NOT recreate a fake logo.

Do NOT invent brand elements.

Do NOT translate the official brand name unless explicitly requested.

The brand should remain visually consistent with the original packaging.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
6. PRODUCT PRESERVATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use the provided product image as the PRIMARY VISUAL SOURCE.

The product is the central visual hero of the entire composition.

Do NOT unnecessarily redesign, deform, replace, recolor, or alter the product packaging.

Preserve:

• exact product shape
• packaging structure
• logo
• brand identity
• printed typography
• label details
• proportions
• colors
• recognizable characteristics
• material appearance

The product must remain immediately recognizable as the exact original product.

If the provided image contains multiple products, preserve the correct number of products.

Do not duplicate products unnecessarily.

Do not generate additional flavors, variants, containers, packages, or accessories unless they are visibly present in the uploaded image.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
7. TEXT GENERATION RULES
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The advertisement may use TWO primary sources of text:

SOURCE A — USER-PROVIDED TEXT

If the user explicitly provides promotional text, CTA, price, offer, slogan, or campaign message, it may be incorporated into the design.

If the user-provided promotional text is in English but the final advertisement is intended for an Arabic-speaking audience, translate it naturally into professional Arabic unless the user explicitly requests English.

SOURCE B — PRODUCT-PACKAGING INFORMATION

The AI may extract factual product information directly from the uploaded packaging.

This includes clearly readable:

• اسم المنتج
• اسم العلامة التجارية
• القيم الغذائية
• مواصفات المنتج
• النكهة
• الوزن
• خصائص المنتج
• الادعاءات المطبوعة

ONLY use information that is clearly supported by the uploaded image or explicitly provided by the user.

All newly generated marketing text must be written in NATURAL, PROFESSIONAL, CORRECT ARABIC.

The copy must feel premium, concise, modern, and commercially appropriate.

Do NOT invent:

• الحقائق الغذائية
• المكونات
• السعرات الحرارية
• نسب البروتين
• الادعاءات الصحية
• الادعاءات الطبية
• الأسعار
• الخصومات
• الشهادات
• الجوائز
• الإحصائيات
• آراء العملاء
• مواصفات المنتج
• ادعاءات الأداء

Do not create marketing claims that are not supported by the packaging or user-provided information.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
8. FACTUAL ACCURACY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

This is CRITICAL.

Every factual product statement in the advertisement must be traceable to either:

1. The uploaded product packaging

OR

2. Information explicitly provided by the user.

Never fill missing information with assumptions.

Never use generic supplement statistics.

Never invent benefits simply because the product belongs to a particular category.

For example:

Do NOT automatically claim:

"يساعد على بناء العضلات"

"يحرق الدهون"

"يعزز هرمون التستوستيرون"

"يحسن الاستشفاء"

"مثبت سريريًا"

"نقي 100%"

"خالي من السكر"

"امتصاص سريع"

unless the claim is explicitly visible on the packaging or explicitly provided by the user.

Accuracy is more important than adding more text.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
9. LANGUAGE HANDLING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The FINAL ADVERTISEMENT must be ARABIC-FIRST.

All newly generated:

• العناوين
• العناوين الفرعية
• الرسائل الترويجية
• عبارات CTA
• النصوص المساندة
• معلومات المنتج
• أوصاف المنتج

must be written in professional Arabic.

Use NATURAL MODERN ARABIC suitable for commercial fitness and nutrition advertising.

Use correct:

• الإملاء
• القواعد
• علامات الترقيم
• الخط العربي
• اتجاه RTL
• التسلسل البصري للنص
• اتصال الحروف العربية

Do NOT generate pseudo-Arabic text.

Do NOT generate meaningless Arabic-like text.

Do NOT reverse Arabic text.

Do NOT mirror Arabic letters incorrectly.

All Arabic text must read naturally from RIGHT TO LEFT.

The visual composition must also respect RTL reading flow.

The viewer's eye should naturally move through the design according to Arabic visual reading direction.

Do NOT introduce unnecessary bilingual text.

English should only remain when it is part of:

• the original product packaging
• the official brand identity
• the official product name
• a user-provided element that the user explicitly wants preserved

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
10. ARABIC MATERIAL-DESIGN COPY STYLE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use short, sophisticated, premium Arabic advertising language.

The copy should feel:

• حديث
• واثق
• مختصر
• طبيعي
• احترافي
• حيوي
• موجه للأداء

Avoid:

• اللغة الإعلانية الرخيصة
• الادعاءات المبالغ فيها
• الجمل الطويلة
• الشعارات غير الضرورية
• علامات الترقيم المفرطة
• علامات التعجب المفرطة
• العبارات التحفيزية المبتذلة

Prefer concise commercial Arabic.

Examples of STYLE only:

"أداء أقوى يبدأ من هنا"

"وقود لأدائك"

"الأداء يبدأ من اختيارك"

"طاقة لكل تمرين"

"ارتقِ بمستواك"

These are examples of tone and structure only.

Do NOT automatically use these phrases unless they are appropriate to the specific product.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
11. CORE MATERIAL DESIGN DIRECTION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a sophisticated PREMIUM MATERIAL DESIGN visual system.

Material Design should be treated as a systematic visual language based on:

• الأسطح الواضحة
• الارتفاع البصري الهادف
• التسلسل الهرمي الواضح
• المسافات المنتظمة
• الخطوط الجريئة
• الألوان الهادفة
• الهندسة البسيطة
• العمق المنضبط
• التنظيم البصري البديهي

Use a strong visual system rather than random UI decoration.

The advertisement should feel inspired by a beautifully designed modern digital interface while remaining clearly a PREMIUM COMMERCIAL PRODUCT ADVERTISEMENT.

Do NOT make the design look like an actual mobile application screenshot.

The interface-inspired language should support the product rather than replace the advertisement.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
12. PRODUCT PRIORITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The product MUST remain more visually important than every Material Design element.

Material Design is the supporting visual system.

The product must remain:

• sharp
• recognizable
• readable
• visually dominant
• physically believable

Do NOT flatten or distort the actual product.

Do NOT turn the product packaging into a UI illustration.

Do NOT replace the product with a digital representation.

The real product image must remain the hero.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
13. VISUAL HIERARCHY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Establish a strict visual hierarchy:

1. PRODUCT
2. اسم المنتج / الرسالة الرئيسية
3. أهم معلومات المنتج
4. العلامة التجارية
5. المعلومات المساندة
6. CTA إذا تم توفيرها

The product must immediately attract attention.

Arabic typography must remain secondary to the product.

UI-inspired surfaces must remain supportive.

The viewer should understand the advertisement within approximately one second.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
14. SURFACE SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a clear hierarchy of visual surfaces.

Use:

• سطح الخلفية
• أسطح المحتوى المرتفعة
• منصة المنتج
• بطاقات المعلومات
• الحاويات البصرية البسيطة
• العناصر العائمة المحدودة

Every surface must have a clear purpose.

Do NOT create cards simply because Material Design uses cards.

Cards should group related information or strengthen hierarchy.

Use rounded corners carefully and consistently.

Avoid excessive rounded rectangles.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
15. ELEVATION SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use a deliberate elevation hierarchy.

Possible levels:

LEVEL 0:
Background surface.

LEVEL 1:
Subtle information containers.

LEVEL 2:
Important information panels.

LEVEL 3:
Primary CTA or featured element.

LEVEL 4:
The PRODUCT as the visual hero.

Elevation must communicate hierarchy.

Use subtle shadows to separate surfaces.

Do NOT make every element appear equally elevated.

Do NOT use exaggerated floating cards.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
16. SHADOW SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use controlled Material Design-inspired shadows.

Shadows should be:

• soft
• subtle
• directional
• consistent
• purposeful

Use shadows primarily to communicate elevation and separation.

Avoid:

• heavy black shadows
• dramatic cinematic shadows
• multiple conflicting light sources
• excessive blur
• glowing edges
• floating-object overload

The product may retain realistic commercial photography shadows.

UI surfaces should use restrained elevation shadows.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
17. COLOR SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Build a disciplined Material-inspired color system around the actual product packaging.

Use:

• اللون الأساسي
• اللون الثانوي
• لون الأسطح
• لون الخلفية
• لون التمييز
• الدرجات المحايدة المساندة

Extract the dominant visual identity from the product.

Use strong color intentionally.

Do NOT introduce unrelated colors.

Avoid rainbow palettes.

Avoid excessive gradients.

If gradients are used, they must be extremely subtle and purposeful.

The product should remain the strongest source of brand color.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
18. PRIMARY COLOR
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Select ONE dominant primary accent derived from the product packaging or brand identity.

Use it strategically for:

• العناوين المهمة
• الخطوط البصرية
• إبراز المعلومات
• CTA
• العناصر الهندسية المحددة

Do not use the primary color everywhere.

Color must communicate hierarchy.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
19. BACKGROUND
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a clean, modern Material-inspired background.

Possible approaches:

• سطح محايد بلون واحد
• سطح فاتح راقٍ
• سطح داكن مستوحى من Material Design
• خلفية لونية هادئة
• مجال لوني منضبط

Choose the background according to the product and brand.

The background must remain visually quiet enough to support the product.

Avoid realistic environments unless explicitly requested.

Do NOT automatically create a gym scene.

Do NOT add random fitness equipment.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
20. PRODUCT PRESENTATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Treat the product as a premium commercial product-photography subject placed within a sophisticated Material Design environment.

Present it with:

• مقياس دقيق
• منظور واقعي
• تموضع دقيق
• تماس طبيعي مع السطح
• فصل بصري منضبط
• ارتفاع بصري خفيف عند الحاجة

The product may be:

• centered
• slightly off-center
• aligned to a grid
• positioned using the rule of thirds
• placed on a subtle elevated surface
• framed by Material-inspired geometry

Choose the strongest placement automatically.

The actual product must remain realistic.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
21. PRODUCT LIGHTING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use premium commercial product photography lighting.

The product must have:

• realistic highlights
• realistic shadows
• accurate material response
• dimensional form
• sharp edges
• realistic contact with the environment

Keep the UI-inspired environment visually consistent with the product lighting.

Do NOT make the product look like a flat digital sticker.

Do NOT over-light the scene.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
22. DEPTH AND DIMENSION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use depth to establish hierarchy, not spectacle.

Create subtle dimensional relationships between:

• الخلفية
• الأسطح
• بطاقات المعلومات
• المنتج
• العناصر الرسومية

Use:

• controlled elevation
• soft shadows
• layering
• overlap
• subtle scale differences

Avoid:

• excessive 3D
• dramatic floating objects
• glassmorphism
• neumorphism
• heavy bevels
• exaggerated perspective

The style must remain distinctly Material Design.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
23. GEOMETRIC SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use simple geometric elements inspired by modern Material visual language.

Possible elements:

• دوائر
• مستطيلات مستديرة
• خطوط
• أشرطة
• أشكال كبسولية
• لوحات هندسية بسيطة
• أشكال تمييز خفيفة

Use them to:

• تأطير المنتج
• توجيه العين
• تنظيم المعلومات
• إنشاء إيقاع بصري
• تعزيز لون العلامة التجارية

Do NOT add decorative geometry without purpose.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
24. INFORMATION CALLOUTS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

When reliable nutritional or product information has been extracted from the packaging, present only the most important values inside clean Material-inspired information surfaces.

Examples:

27 غ
بروتين

109
سعرة حرارية

86%
بروتين

1 كغ

These are ONLY examples of formatting.

Do not automatically use these numbers unless they are actually visible on the uploaded product packaging.

Information may be presented using:

• بطاقات مرتفعة
• لوحات معلومات مدمجة
• كتل أرقام واضحة
• مؤشرات دائرية
• فواصل بسيطة
• تسميات منظمة

Keep them concise.

Do not create a dashboard.

Do not display too many numbers.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
25. CTA DESIGN
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

If the user provides a CTA, price, offer, or promotional action, present it as a clear Material-inspired interactive element.

Possible treatment:

• زر مرتفع بصريًا
• زر بسيط بشكل كبسولة
• سطح إجراء مستطيل
• كتلة لونية بارزة

The CTA must be visually important but must NOT compete with the product.

Do NOT invent a CTA if none is provided or appropriate.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
26. DISTRACTION CONTROL
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

THIS IS CRITICAL.

Material Design can easily become an unnecessary UI mockup.

Avoid that.

The advertisement must remain extremely easy on the eyes.

DO NOT add:

• random cards
• excessive cards
• fake app navigation
• fake menus
• fake tabs
• fake switches
• fake sliders
• random buttons
• random icons
• dashboards
• navigation bars
• status bars
• random gym equipment
• random dumbbells
• random weights
• bodybuilding silhouettes
• unrelated athletes
• excessive gradients
• excessive shadows
• excessive circles
• excessive UI elements
• fake statistics
• fake product claims
• fake certifications
• visual clutter

Do NOT make the design look like a mobile application.

The viewer must immediately understand that this is a PRODUCT ADVERTISEMENT.

If an element does not improve the product presentation, REMOVE IT.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
27. ARABIC TYPOGRAPHY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use premium modern Arabic typography.

Typography should be:

• clean
• bold
• highly readable
• modern
• systematic
• confident
• professionally balanced

Prefer professional Arabic sans-serif typography such as:

• Cairo
• IBM Plex Sans Arabic
• DIN Next Arabic style
• modern geometric Arabic sans-serif
• clean contemporary Arabic typography

Use no more than TWO typefaces.

Create a strong typographic hierarchy using:

• العنوان الرئيسي
• العنوان الفرعي
• الرقم أو القيمة الغذائية
• التسمية
• CTA

All typography must follow RIGHT-TO-LEFT (RTL) direction.

Maintain proper:

• اتصال الحروف العربية
• المحاذاة
• المسافات بين الأسطر
• المسافات بين الكلمات
• التسلسل الهرمي
• المحاذاة من اليمين

Do NOT use:

• الخطوط العربية الزخرفية
• الخطوط الطفولية
• الخط العربي المفرط في الزخرفة
• النص العربي المشوه
• النص العربي المعكوس
• النص المتوهج
• النص المعدني
• التدرجات المفرطة
• الحدود المفرطة
• تأثيرات النص المبالغ فيها

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
28. TEXT DENSITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Keep the amount of text LOW.

This is a premium commercial advertisement, NOT a product catalog, nutrition label, or application screen.

Do not copy the entire back label into the design.

Do not display every ingredient or nutritional value.

Select only the strongest, most useful information.

Prioritize:

• visual impact
• immediate comprehension
• product recognition
• readability
• structured hierarchy
• premium presentation

Use short Arabic labels and concise information.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
29. FITNESS / NUTRITION VISUAL LANGUAGE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Communicate fitness through:

• الأداء
• الدقة
• القوة
• الطاقة
• الانضباط
• التكنولوجيا الحديثة
• العافية
• نمط الحياة الرياضي

Material Design should reinforce a sense of:

الأداء العصري.

The visual system should feel organized, efficient, intelligent, and contemporary.

Do not automatically add gym equipment.

Do not automatically add athletes.

Do not use bodybuilding clichés unless explicitly requested.

The product itself should communicate the fitness or nutrition category whenever possible.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
30. NEGATIVE SPACE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Maintain generous and intentional negative space.

Use empty space to:

• isolate the product
• strengthen hierarchy
• improve readability
• separate surfaces
• create premium perception
• reduce visual fatigue

Do not fill empty areas with additional UI elements.

Empty space is part of the design system.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
31. COMPOSITION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use professional Material-inspired composition principles.

Possible approaches:

• centered hero
• asymmetric editorial layout
• product-focused card hierarchy
• structured grid
• rule-of-thirds
• vertical product emphasis
• layered surface composition
• strong color-accent composition

Choose the strongest composition automatically based on the product image and extracted information.

Do not mechanically follow a template.

The composition must feel custom-designed for the specific product.

Maintain a consistent RTL visual flow.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
32. GRID AND SPACING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use a disciplined spacing system.

Maintain:

• consistent margins
• consistent padding
• consistent gaps
• precise alignment
• proportional relationships
• visual rhythm

Use a clear modular grid.

Information cards should share consistent dimensions and spacing.

Do not randomly position UI-inspired elements.

The composition should feel systematic without becoming rigid.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
33. BRANDING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

If a brand name or logo is clearly visible on the product:

Integrate it subtly and professionally.

Do not overpower the product.

Do not redesign the logo.

Do not recreate a fake logo.

Do not invent brand elements.

Do not translate the official brand name unless explicitly requested.

Maintain visual consistency with the original packaging.

The brand should feel naturally integrated into the Material Design system.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
34. PREMIUM COMMERCIAL QUALITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The final advertisement should feel suitable for:

• premium sports nutrition brands
• luxury fitness brands
• modern wellness companies
• high-end supplement companies
• athletic technology brands
• premium performance brands
• professional Arabic commercial campaigns

Think:

LUXURY FITNESS BRANDING

*

PREMIUM SPORTS NUTRITION

*

HIGH-END MATERIAL DESIGN

*

MODERN DIGITAL PRODUCT DESIGN

*

ARABIC COMMERCIAL ART DIRECTION

*

COMMERCIAL PRODUCT PHOTOGRAPHY

*

EDITORIAL ART DIRECTION

Do NOT make it look like:

• a generic AI poster
• a cheap supplement advertisement
• a mobile app screenshot
• a dashboard
• a UI mockup
• a generic Google template
• a gaming poster
• a bodybuilding poster
• a crowded Instagram template
• a generic Canva design

The design should feel premium, modern, systematic, and commercially intentional.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
35. IMAGE QUALITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Prioritize extremely high visual quality.

The final artwork must have:

• photorealistic product presentation
• accurate packaging
• sharp product details
• clean UI-inspired geometry
• crisp edges
• precise Arabic typography
• accurate color relationships
• realistic product lighting
• controlled elevation
• professional composition
• polished Arabic typography
• premium art direction
• commercial-quality finish

Avoid:

• warped packaging
• distorted logos
• duplicated products
• malformed objects
• unreadable Arabic text
• incorrect Arabic typography
• inconsistent geometry
• sloppy alignment
• excessive UI elements
• excessive shadows
• excessive gradients
• AI artifacts
• invented product information

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
36. FINAL ART-DIRECTION CHECK
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Before finalizing the artwork, evaluate it as a professional Arabic commercial Material Design art director.

Ask:

Is the product immediately recognizable?

Is the product the strongest visual element?

Did the product analysis use only information actually visible in the uploaded image?

Are all nutritional values and specifications accurate?

Did the design avoid invented claims?

Is all newly generated text in natural, correct Arabic?

Does the typography follow proper RTL composition?

Is the Arabic typography professionally typeset?

Is the visual hierarchy immediately understandable?

Does the elevation system communicate hierarchy?

Are the cards purposeful?

Are the surfaces organized?

Are the colors controlled?

Are there too many UI elements?

Does the design look like an advertisement rather than an application?

Is there enough negative space?

Does the composition feel genuinely Material Design?

Does it look premium rather than generic?

Does the product feel premium?

Does the composition feel professionally art-directed?

Would a real premium fitness or nutrition brand publish this?

If removing an element makes the composition stronger, REMOVE IT.

The final design must feel:

MODERN.
CLEAN.
STRUCTURED.
PREMIUM.
FUNCTIONAL.
CONFIDENT.
POLISHED.
INTUITIVE.
DIMENSIONAL.
BALANCED.
ARABIC-FIRST.
COMMERCIAL.
EASY ON THE EYES.

The goal is NOT to demonstrate how many UI elements can be added.

The goal is to use Material Design principles to create an exceptionally clear, structured, premium product advertisement.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
37. FINAL OUTPUT
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Generate ONE finished advertisement.

Do not generate multiple variations.

Do not show sketches.

Do not show wireframes.

Do not provide explanations.

Analyze the uploaded product image first.

Extract the reliable product information.

Select the most valuable information.

Determine the appropriate Arabic copy.

Design the composition using the specified Material Design art direction.

Then generate the final polished commercial artwork directly.

The final visible advertisement should be primarily Arabic and follow a strict RTL visual structure.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
38. ASPECT RATIO — CHANGE ONLY THIS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

FINAL ASPECT RATIO:

9:16 VERTICAL PORTRAIT

Design the entire composition specifically for this aspect ratio from the beginning.

Do NOT create another aspect ratio and crop it afterward.

Do NOT stretch, squeeze, or distort the composition.

All visual elements must be intentionally positioned for the specified vertical format.

Maintain safe margins around the product, Arabic typography, logo, information cards, CTA, and all important elements.

The final artwork must be a true 9:16 vertical composition optimized for Instagram Stories, Reels, and vertical social-media presentation.

prompts.title: Brutalism  En
prompts.promptText:
Create a premium commercial FITNESS / NUTRITION advertisement using a STRICT, SOPHISTICATED, HIGH-END BRUTALISM DESIGN STYLE.

The final artwork must be designed specifically for an ENGLISH-SPEAKING AUDIENCE.

English must be the PRIMARY visual language of the final advertisement.

The entire composition must follow a natural LEFT-TO-RIGHT (LTR) visual and typographic flow.

The final artwork must look like it was created by an elite commercial art director, premium fitness brand designer, professional product photographer, contemporary graphic designer, brutalist art director, typography specialist, and high-end visual communication designer working together.

The result must feel:

BOLD.
RAW.
DIRECT.
UNAPOLOGETIC.
POWERFUL.
MODERN.
INDUSTRIAL.
EDITORIAL.
GRAPHIC.
HIGH-CONTRAST.
CONFIDENT.
PREMIUM.
COMMERCIAL.
EASY TO UNDERSTAND.

This is NOT a generic "dark fitness poster."

Do NOT simply use black backgrounds, oversized text, and random distressed textures.

Create a genuine, professionally art-directed BRUTALIST composition based on raw visual hierarchy, deliberate asymmetry, oversized typography, exposed structure, hard geometric forms, aggressive scale contrast, controlled imperfection, strong contrast, unconventional alignment, and uncompromising visual clarity.

The PRODUCT remains the HERO.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1. PRODUCT INPUT
   ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

PRODUCT IMAGE:

[INSERT PRODUCT IMAGE]

The uploaded product image is the PRIMARY SOURCE OF TRUTH.

The image must be analyzed before creating the advertisement.

Do NOT require the user to manually provide product information if it can be reliably extracted from the uploaded image.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
2. PRODUCT IMAGE ANALYSIS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Before designing the advertisement, carefully inspect the uploaded product image.

Identify and extract ONLY information that is clearly visible and reliably readable from the product packaging.

Analyze:

• Product name
• Product type
• Brand name
• Flavor
• Net weight
• Serving size
• Protein amount per serving
• Calories per serving
• Protein percentage
• Carbohydrates
• Fat
• Ingredients
• Key nutritional information
• Product features
• Product claims
• Certifications
• Any other clearly printed product information

The uploaded packaging is the authoritative source.

Do NOT invent, assume, estimate, infer, or fabricate product information.

If information is partially visible but cannot be read with confidence, DO NOT use it.

If information is completely absent from the image, DO NOT create it.

If nutritional information is visible, preserve the exact factual values and units shown on the packaging.

Do not convert, reinterpret, round, or modify numerical values unless explicitly requested.

For example:

If the package says:

"27g Protein"

use:

"27g Protein"

If it says:

"109 kcal"

use:

"109 kcal"

If it says:

"1 KG"

use:

"1 KG"

The factual numerical value must remain unchanged.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
3. INFORMATION SELECTION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

After analyzing the product image, automatically determine which extracted information is most valuable for a premium Brutalism commercial advertisement.

Prioritize:

1. Product name
2. Brand name
3. Most important nutritional value
4. Key product specification
5. Net weight
6. Flavor, if relevant
7. One or two important product features

Do NOT attempt to display every piece of information extracted from the packaging.

This is a PREMIUM ADVERTISEMENT, not a nutrition facts sheet.

Select only the information that improves the advertisement.

Use concise English visual callouts instead of paragraphs.

Only use nutritional values and specifications that are actually visible and readable in the uploaded image.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
4. PRODUCT TITLE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Automatically determine the product title from the uploaded packaging.

Use the exact recognizable product name printed on the packaging whenever possible.

Do NOT invent a new product name.

Do NOT unnecessarily rewrite the brand or product name.

If the official product name is clearly written in English, preserve it accurately.

If a generic descriptive phrase can be naturally presented in English without changing the product identity, use professional wording.

If the product title is unclear, use only the clearly readable portion.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
5. BRAND IDENTIFICATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Automatically identify the brand from the packaging if clearly visible.

Preserve the original logo and brand identity.

Do NOT redesign the logo.

Do NOT recreate a fake logo.

Do NOT invent brand elements.

The brand should remain visually consistent with the original packaging.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
6. PRODUCT PRESERVATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use the provided product image as the PRIMARY VISUAL SOURCE.

The product is the central visual hero of the entire composition.

Do NOT unnecessarily redesign, deform, replace, recolor, or alter the product packaging.

Preserve:

• exact product shape
• packaging structure
• logo
• brand identity
• printed typography
• label details
• proportions
• colors
• recognizable characteristics
• material appearance

The product must remain immediately recognizable as the exact original product.

If the provided image contains multiple products, preserve the correct number of products.

Do not duplicate products unnecessarily.

Do not generate additional flavors, variants, containers, packages, or accessories unless they are visibly present in the uploaded image.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
7. TEXT GENERATION RULES
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The advertisement may use TWO primary sources of text:

SOURCE A — USER-PROVIDED TEXT

If the user explicitly provides promotional text, CTA, price, offer, slogan, or campaign message, it may be incorporated into the design.

SOURCE B — PRODUCT-PACKAGING INFORMATION

The AI may extract factual product information directly from the uploaded packaging.

This includes clearly readable:

• Product name
• Brand name
• Nutritional values
• Product specifications
• Flavor
• Weight
• Product features
• Printed claims

ONLY use information that is clearly supported by the uploaded image or explicitly provided by the user.

All newly generated marketing text must be written in NATURAL, PROFESSIONAL ENGLISH.

The copy must feel premium, concise, modern, direct, and commercially appropriate.

Do NOT invent:

• nutritional facts
• ingredients
• calories
• protein percentages
• health claims
• medical claims
• prices
• discounts
• certifications
• awards
• statistics
• testimonials
• product specifications
• performance claims

Do not create marketing claims that are not supported by the packaging or user-provided information.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
8. FACTUAL ACCURACY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

This is CRITICAL.

Every factual product statement in the advertisement must be traceable to either:

1. The uploaded product packaging

OR

2. Information explicitly provided by the user.

Never fill missing information with assumptions.

Never use generic supplement statistics.

Never invent benefits simply because the product belongs to a particular category.

For example:

Do NOT automatically claim:

"Builds Muscle"

"Burns Fat"

"Boosts Testosterone"

"Improves Recovery"

"Clinically Proven"

"100% Pure"

"Zero Sugar"

"Fast Absorption"

unless the claim is explicitly visible on the packaging or explicitly provided by the user.

Accuracy is more important than adding more text.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
9. LANGUAGE HANDLING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The FINAL ADVERTISEMENT must be ENGLISH-FIRST.

All newly generated:

• headlines
• subtitles
• promotional messages
• CTAs
• supporting text
• product information callouts
• descriptive text

must be written in professional English.

Use NATURAL MODERN ENGLISH suitable for commercial fitness and nutrition advertising.

Use correct:

• spelling
• grammar
• punctuation
• capitalization
• typography
• LTR direction
• text hierarchy

Do NOT generate pseudo-English text.

Do NOT generate meaningless text.

Do NOT reverse text.

Do NOT mirror letters incorrectly.

All English text must read naturally from LEFT TO RIGHT.

The visual composition must also respect LTR reading flow.

Do NOT introduce unnecessary bilingual text.

English should remain the dominant language throughout the advertisement.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
10. BRUTALIST COPY STYLE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use short, powerful, sophisticated English advertising language.

The copy should feel:

• direct
• confident
• sharp
• modern
• minimal
• energetic
• performance-oriented

Prefer short statements and powerful word combinations.

Examples of STYLE only:

"BUILT FOR PERFORMANCE"

"NO EXCUSES."

"TRAIN HARD."

"POWER YOUR PERFORMANCE"

"MADE TO PERFORM"

"YOUR NEXT LEVEL."

These are examples of tone and structure only.

Do NOT automatically use these phrases unless they are appropriate to the specific product.

Avoid:

• long marketing paragraphs
• motivational clichés
• exaggerated claims
• corporate language
• excessive slogans
• excessive punctuation
• unnecessary decorative copy

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
11. CORE BRUTALISM DIRECTION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a sophisticated PREMIUM BRUTALIST visual system.

The design should intentionally expose its visual structure rather than hiding it.

Use:

• oversized typography
• bold geometric blocks
• hard-edged shapes
• raw grids
• visible alignment systems
• asymmetric layouts
• strong contrast
• unconventional cropping
• intentional overlap
• oversized numbers
• editorial tension
• controlled visual imperfection
• stark graphic elements
• abrupt scale changes

The design should feel deliberately raw and uncompromising.

It should appear highly designed, not unfinished.

Do NOT confuse Brutalism with poor design.

The result must be precise, intentional, and professionally controlled.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
12. PRODUCT PRIORITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The product MUST remain more visually important than every Brutalist graphic element.

Brutalism is the supporting visual language.

The product must remain:

• sharp
• recognizable
• readable
• visually dominant
• physically believable

Do NOT turn the product into a graphic illustration.

Do NOT distort the packaging to make it "more brutalist."

Do NOT cover the product with oversized typography.

Typography may overlap or interact with the product only when readability and product recognition remain intact.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
13. VISUAL HIERARCHY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Establish a strict visual hierarchy:

1. PRODUCT
2. PRIMARY HEADLINE / PRODUCT TITLE
3. KEY PRODUCT INFORMATION
4. BRAND
5. SUPPORTING INFORMATION
6. CTA, if provided

The product must immediately attract attention.

Typography may be visually aggressive, but it must not destroy product recognition.

The viewer should understand the advertisement within approximately one second.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
14. TYPOGRAPHIC SCALE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Typography is one of the PRIMARY visual elements of the Brutalist composition.

Use dramatic scale contrast.

Possible hierarchy:

• extremely large headline
• medium product name
• compact information
• small metadata
• oversized numeric values

Use typography at different scales to create tension.

Allow some typography to extend close to the edges of the composition.

Allow intentional cropping only when it does not harm readability.

Do NOT make every text element large.

The contrast between large and small typography is essential.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
15. GRID SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use a strong editorial grid.

The grid may be visible or implied.

Use:

• columns
• modular blocks
• alignment lines
• strict margins
• intentional offsets
• asymmetrical placement

The design may deliberately break the grid in selected areas.

However, the underlying structure must remain controlled.

Do NOT randomly scatter elements.

Controlled disruption is the goal.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
16. ASYMMETRY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use deliberate asymmetry.

Avoid overly centered compositions unless the product strongly benefits from a centered hero.

Possible approaches:

• product shifted to one side
• oversized headline occupying another area
• information block offset from the main axis
• cropped geometric elements
• uneven visual weight
• diagonal or vertical tension

The composition should feel energetic and contemporary.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
17. COLOR SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Build the color system around the actual product packaging and brand identity.

Prefer a restrained but powerful palette.

Possible structure:

• one dominant background color
• product colors
• one strong accent
• black or white typography where appropriate

Strong combinations may include:

• black + white + one accent
• off-white + black + one accent
• saturated accent + neutral
• dark neutral + high-contrast typography

Do not use many unrelated colors.

Do not automatically use black.

Brutalism can use any color palette as long as the visual system remains bold and controlled.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
18. BACKGROUND
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a bold but controlled Brutalist background.

Possible approaches:

• solid color
• raw paper-like field
• stark monochrome surface
• strong color block
• high-contrast editorial background
• subtle industrial texture

Texture, if used, must remain restrained.

Avoid:

• excessive grunge
• dirty textures
• fake concrete everywhere
• random graffiti
• excessive noise
• smoke
• fire
• explosions

The background must support the product.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
19. PRODUCT PRESENTATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Treat the product as a premium commercial product-photography subject placed inside an aggressive graphic composition.

Present it with:

• accurate scale
• realistic perspective
• sharp details
• controlled grounding
• strong visual separation

The product may be:

• large and dominant
• slightly off-center
• vertically positioned
• framed by typography
• partially surrounded by geometric blocks
• positioned against a high-contrast field

Choose the strongest placement automatically.

The product itself must remain realistic.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
20. PRODUCT LIGHTING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use premium commercial product photography lighting.

The product must have:

• realistic highlights
• realistic shadows
• accurate material response
• dimensional form
• sharp edges
• realistic contact with the environment

Lighting should remain clean and controlled.

Do NOT use excessive cinematic lighting.

Do NOT make the product overly glossy.

The product should look premium and physically real.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
21. DEPTH AND SHADOW
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Brutalism should rely primarily on:

• scale
• contrast
• geometry
• typography
• composition

rather than complex 3D effects.

Use shadows sparingly.

If shadows are used, they should be:

• hard or controlled
• minimal
• purposeful
• consistent

Avoid:

• excessive soft shadows
• floating 3D objects
• glassmorphism
• neumorphism
• excessive gradients
• glossy 3D effects

The design must remain distinctly Brutalist.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
22. GRAPHIC ELEMENTS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use a restrained collection of graphic elements.

Possible elements:

• thick lines
• blocks
• rectangles
• circles
• oversized numbers
• arrows
• bars
• cropped shapes
• simple symbols
• editorial markers
• technical labels

Every graphic element must have a purpose.

Do NOT decorate every empty area.

Use visual tension through scale and placement rather than quantity.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
23. INFORMATION CALLOUTS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

When reliable nutritional or product information has been extracted from the packaging, present only the most important values as bold Brutalist information blocks.

Examples:

27g
PROTEIN

109
KCAL

86%
PROTEIN

1 KG

These are ONLY examples of formatting.

Do not automatically use these numbers unless they are actually visible on the uploaded product packaging.

Information may be presented using:

• oversized numbers
• compact labels
• bold blocks
• high-contrast panels
• technical-style metadata
• strong dividers

Keep them concise.

Do not turn the advertisement into an infographic.

Do not display too many numbers.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
24. DISTRACTION CONTROL
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

THIS IS CRITICAL.

Brutalism can easily become chaotic.

Avoid that.

The advertisement must remain extremely easy on the eyes despite its aggressive visual language.

DO NOT add:

• excessive grunge
• random textures
• excessive distressed effects
• random graffiti
• excessive typography
• dozens of labels
• random arrows
• random numbers
• fake technical information
• random geometric shapes
• random gym equipment
• random dumbbells
• random weights
• bodybuilding silhouettes
• unrelated athletes
• smoke
• fire
• explosions
• lightning
• excessive particles
• fake statistics
• fake product claims
• fake certifications
• visual clutter

Do NOT confuse chaos with Brutalism.

The composition should feel controlled, intentional, and highly art-directed.

If an element does not improve the product presentation, REMOVE IT.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
25. NEGATIVE SPACE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Maintain deliberate negative space.

Brutalism does NOT mean filling every area.

Use empty space to create:

• tension
• contrast
• hierarchy
• breathing room
• visual impact

A large empty area beside an oversized headline or product can be extremely powerful.

Do not fill negative space simply because it exists.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
26. COMPOSITION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Use professional Brutalist editorial composition.

Possible approaches:

• oversized central hero
• asymmetric editorial layout
• product on one side + oversized typography on the other
• aggressive vertical composition
• diagonal tension
• modular grid
• cropped typography
• strong geometric framing

Choose the strongest composition automatically based on the product image and extracted information.

Do not mechanically follow a template.

The composition must feel custom-designed for the specific product.

Maintain a consistent LTR visual flow.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
27. BRANDING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

If a brand name or logo is clearly visible on the product:

Integrate it subtly and professionally.

Do not overpower the product.

Do not redesign the logo.

Do not recreate a fake logo.

Do not invent brand elements.

Maintain visual consistency with the original packaging.

The Brutalist visual system must support the brand rather than destroy its identity.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
28. PREMIUM COMMERCIAL QUALITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The final advertisement should feel suitable for:

• premium sports nutrition brands
• luxury fitness brands
• modern athletic companies
• high-end supplement companies
• performance brands
• streetwear-inspired fitness brands
• professional commercial campaigns

Think:

LUXURY FITNESS BRANDING

*

PREMIUM SPORTS NUTRITION

*

HIGH-END BRUTALIST GRAPHIC DESIGN

*

EDITORIAL ART DIRECTION

*

COMMERCIAL PRODUCT PHOTOGRAPHY

*

CONTEMPORARY SPORTS CULTURE

Do NOT make it look like:

• a generic AI poster
• a cheap supplement advertisement
• a random grunge poster
• an amateur punk flyer
• a gaming poster
• a bodybuilding cliché poster
• a messy collage
• a generic Canva design
• an unfinished graphic design

The design should feel raw but expensive.

Aggressive but controlled.

Minimal but powerful.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
29. IMAGE QUALITY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Prioritize extremely high visual quality.

The final artwork must have:

• photorealistic product presentation
• accurate packaging
• sharp product details
• crisp geometric elements
• strong typographic rendering
• precise alignment
• controlled contrast
• professional composition
• polished English typography
• premium art direction
• commercial-quality finish

Avoid:

• warped packaging
• distorted logos
• duplicated products
• malformed objects
• unreadable text
• inconsistent geometry
• sloppy alignment
• random colors
• excessive grunge
• excessive effects
• AI artifacts
• invented product information

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
30. FINAL ART-DIRECTION CHECK
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Before finalizing the artwork, evaluate it as a professional commercial Brutalist art director.

Ask:

Is the product immediately recognizable?

Is the product the strongest visual element?

Did the product analysis use only information actually visible in the uploaded image?

Are all nutritional values and specifications accurate?

Did the design avoid invented claims?

Is all newly generated text in natural, correct English?

Does the typography follow proper LTR composition?

Is the typography bold without becoming unreadable?

Is the asymmetry intentional?

Is the grid controlled?

Are the graphic elements purposeful?

Is the color palette restrained?

Is there enough negative space?

Does the design feel Brutalist rather than merely dark or grungy?

Does it feel raw but premium?

Does it feel aggressive but controlled?

Does the product feel premium?

Does the composition feel professionally art-directed?

Would a real premium fitness or nutrition brand publish this?

If removing an element makes the composition stronger, REMOVE IT.

The final design must feel:

BOLD.
RAW.
DIRECT.
UNAPOLOGETIC.
POWERFUL.
MODERN.
INDUSTRIAL.
EDITORIAL.
GRAPHIC.
HIGH-CONTRAST.
CONFIDENT.
PREMIUM.
COMMERCIAL.
EASY TO UNDERSTAND.

The goal is NOT to create visual chaos.

The goal is to create controlled visual aggression with exceptional clarity.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
31. FINAL OUTPUT
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Generate ONE finished advertisement.

Do not generate multiple variations.

Do not show sketches.

Do not show wireframes.

Do not provide explanations.

Analyze the uploaded product image first.

Extract the reliable product information.

Select the most valuable information.

Determine the appropriate English copy.

Design the composition using the specified Brutalism art direction.

Then generate the final polished commercial artwork directly.

The final visible advertisement should be primarily English and follow a strict LTR visual structure.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
32. ASPECT RATIO — CHANGE ONLY THIS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

FINAL ASPECT RATIO:

9:16 VERTICAL PORTRAIT

Design the entire composition specifically for this aspect ratio from the beginning.

Do NOT create another aspect ratio and crop it afterward.

Do NOT stretch, squeeze, or distort the composition.

All visual elements must be intentionally positioned for the specified vertical format.

Maintain safe margins around the product, English typography, logo, information blocks, and all important elements.

The final artwork must be a true 9:16 vertical composition optimized for Instagram Stories, Reels, and vertical social-media presentation.

prompts.title: Brutalism  Ar
prompts.promptText:
Create a premium commercial FITNESS / NUTRITION advertisement using a STRICT, SOPHISTICATED, HIGH-END BRUTALISM DESIGN STYLE.

The final artwork must be designed specifically for an ARABIC-SPEAKING AUDIENCE.

Arabic must be the PRIMARY visual language of the final advertisement.

The entire composition must follow a natural RIGHT-TO-LEFT (RTL) visual and typographic flow.

The final artwork must look like it was created by an elite commercial art director, premium fitness brand designer, professional product photographer, contemporary graphic designer, Brutalist art director, Arabic typography specialist, and high-end visual communication designer working together.

The result must feel:

BOLD.
RAW.
DIRECT.
